Finally, we propose a minimum acquisition and dataset specification, tiered by clinical setting from research to community screening, and a staged roadmap that combines hardware standardisation (focus-stacked, illumination-controlled, colour-calibrated acquisition), interoperable metadata-rich storage (DICOM where infrastructure permits), quantitative phenotype definition, and diverse international dataset collaborations, so that the ocular surface can benefit from quantitative imaging and AI as other areas of ophthalmology have begun to.

items.title: An astrocyte-microglia MFG-E8 axis promotes synapse engulfment in early amyloid pathology.
items.abstract: Region-specific synapse loss is an early hallmark of Alzheimer's disease, yet the upstream signals that render synapses vulnerable remain unclear. In a mouse model of amyloidosis, we identify an early astrocyte state that emerges in vulnerable brain regions before widespread plaque deposition and overt gliosis. These astrocytes exhibit bulbous-looking perisynaptic processes enriched in p62 and glycogen, impaired autophagic flux and calcium signaling, and diminished astrocyte-synapse coverage. Rather than exhibiting increased synapse engulfment, bulbous astrocytes show elevated milk fat globule-epidermal growth factor 8 (MFG-E8) and are associated with increased local microglial synapse engulfment. Astrocyte-specific gain- and loss-of-function experiments demonstrate that astrocyte-derived MFG-E8 is required for microglial synapse engulfment and acts through microglial β3 integrin signaling. Astrocytic Mfge8 deletion reduces microglial engulfment and synapse loss across amyloidosis models and is associated with reduced amyloid pathology, gliosis, and cognitive impairment. Together, these findings define an astrocyte-microglia MFG-E8 signaling axis that contributes to region-specific synaptic vulnerability during early amyloid pathology.

items.title: Mechanosensitive YAP-RUNX1 signaling drives TH1 cell dysfunction and tumor immunosuppression.
items.abstract: Tissue stiffening is a predominant malignant physical alteration in cancer progression, yet its effect on specific immune subsets within the tumor microenvironment is not well defined. Here we show that elevated tissue stiffness subverts tumor-infiltrating type 1 helper T (TH1) cells to drive immunosuppression in pancreatic cancer. Mechanistically, stiffness triggers integrin-mediated mechanotransduction to activate YAP, which translocates to the nucleus and cooperates with RUNX1 to transcriptionally upregulate a set of dysfunction-associated genes. These reprogrammed TH1 cells acquire a distinct dysfunction-associated secretory phenotype, which in turn drives M2-like polarization of macrophages and amplifies local immunosuppression. Notably, inhibiting YAP expression or disrupting YAP-RUNX1 interaction reverses the dysfunctional state of TH1 cells and restores antitumor immunity. These findings delineate a mechano-immunological mechanism by which tumor stiffness subverts TH1 cell functions, indicating a possible therapeutic avenue to alleviate immunosuppression and potentiate immunotherapy efficacy in stiff tumors.

items.title: Development of a Quantitative Contrast CT-Based TAVR-Risk Score to Reliably Predict Deformation in Bicuspid Aortic Valves.

sections.objective: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) calcification affects clinical outcomes by causing transcatheter heart valve (THV) deformation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, a computed tomography (CT)-based scoring system for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation has not been established. This study sought to develop a cardiac CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation.
sections.methods: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with BAV who underwent TAVR using contemporary balloon-expandable valves between January 2016 and December 2024 and who had preprocedural and postprocedural CT imaging. The BAV TAVR-risk score integrated calcification severity and distribution across valve leaflets, raphe, annulus, and left ventricular outflow tract, quantified using a fixed HU-850 threshold of detection on contrast-enhanced CT scans. Score thresholds were derived by receiver operating curve analysis with Youden index optimization. Patients were categorized into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk score groups.
sections.results: Among 321 patients (median follow-up: 1,825 days; Q1-Q3: 765-1,825 days), 56 (17.4%) were classified into the high-risk score group. Both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV occurred in 49 of the 321 patients (15.3%) and were predominantly observed in the high-risk score group. However, in the low-risk score group, 149 of 155 patients (96.1%) demonstrated no underexpansion or eccentricity of the THV. A high BAV TAVR-risk score independently predicted both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV (OR: 89.13; 95% CI: 35.02-226.83; P < 0.001).
sections.conclusion: This CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score provides a systematic method to precisely quantify BAV severity which reliably predicts THV deformation for BAV patients with contemporary balloon-expandable valves and may help guide decision-making in this challenging population.

items.title: Naegleria fowleri in a warming world: epidemiology, genotypic distribution, management challenges, and priorities for public health action.
items.abstract: Naegleria fowleri causes primary amoebic meningoencephalitis, a fatal infection with profound implications for global health burden and water safety. Rising global temperatures and ageing water infrastructure are expanding the ecological range of this pathogen, increasing exposure risk in both high-income and resource-constrained settings. The infection mainly occurs through contact with warm freshwater and brackish waters and inhalation of cyst-laden dust; however, surveillance systems remain fragmented and under-resourced, particularly in low-income and middle-income countries. Diagnosis is often delayed or made post-mortem, and survival is exceedingly rare. In this Review, we synthesised the current knowledge on global epidemiology, genotypic distribution, and environmental drivers of N fowleri emergence and identified key gaps in monitoring, water treatment, and governance. We propose that climate-resilient water safety strategies, integrated surveillance, and cross-sectoral collaboration are urgently needed to mitigate the risk of Nfowleri exposure and to minimise future cases of primary amoebic meningoencephalitis. Strengthening global health systems to address this emerging threat will require coordinated investment, policy innovation, and research to close knowledge gaps and protect clinically vulnerable populations.

items.title: The IgG4ward! Foundation guidelines on the treatment of IgG4-related disease.
items.abstract: IgG4-related disease is a chronic, immune-mediated, systemic condition that presents as tumour-like masses. Since publication of the last international consensus statement on the treatment of IgG4-related disease in 2015, the related literature has expanded considerably, with two phase 3, randomised, placebo-controlled trials published within the past 2 years. This foundation of evidence for treatment decisions justified new, dedicated treatment guidelines. 62 investigators-comprising 52 physicians, one medical reference librarian, eight patients, and one caregiver from 15 countries across six continents-were assembled to form a treatment guidelines group. The physicians had a broad range of specialties and patient representation spanned the full spectrum of organ involvement. The treatment guidelines group generated 183 candidate questions, which were consolidated into 40 final questions approved by the IgG4ward! Advisory Board. These questions formed the basis of a systematic literature search, led by a medical reference librarian, which informed the development of 28 treatment statements. Supporting evidence for each statement was independently graded using the 2011 Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine Levels of Evidence framework. The 52 physicians voted electronically on their level of agreement with each statement; consensus required more than 80% to agree or strongly agree with the statement, and was reached for 22 of the 28 statements. The evidence base reflects marked recent progress due to the publication of phase 3 clinical trials, although most statements still rely on low-level evidence. This effort provides cohesive, consensus-based guidelines from a geographically and professionally diverse group of experts in IgG4-related disease, reflecting the evolution in the field since 2015. Despite this progress, important knowledge gaps remain, and are highlighted to guide future research.

items.title: Prioritising malaria interventions to maximise health: the role of economic evaluation.
items.abstract: Malaria decision makers face difficult choices about how to allocate scarce resources to complex intervention packages across heterogeneous areas and populations. Such decisions must balance competing objectives, including health maximisation, equity, and political acceptability. The current WHO-supported subnational tailoring process improves on uniform national planning by targeting interventions to local contexts based on determinants of malaria risk. However, the WHO guidance does not provide a transparent, systematic framework for weighing the health benefits of malaria interventions against the resources required, within budget constraints. Health economic evaluation, the science of maximising health with finite resources, should be central to malaria decision making, thereby informing decision makers about health-maximising choices even when other considerations take precedence. We propose improvements, including a revised prioritisation approach explicitly informed by economic evaluation principles. We also discuss how research activities can better support health maximisation and how all stakeholders can contribute to improving malaria priority setting.

items.title: Left Bundle-Branch Pacing versus Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block.

sections.objective: Right ventricular pacing is associated with cardiac dyssynchrony and left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Left bundle-branch pacing preserves left ventricular electrical and mechanical synchrony, but its clinical benefits relative to right ventricular pacing in patients with atrioventricular block remain unclear.
sections.methods: In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned patients with atrioventricular block in a 1:1 ratio to receive left bundle-branch pacing or right ventricular pacing. The primary outcome was a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy.
sections.results: A total of 702 patients underwent randomization, with 348 assigned to receive left bundle-branch pacing and 354 to receive right ventricular pacing; 17 patients (6 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 11 in the right ventricular pacing group) were excluded before device implantation. A total of 685 patients (342 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 343 in the right ventricular pacing group) were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. The mean age of the patients was 68.4 years, and 57.5% were men. At the prespecified interim analysis, the data monitoring committee recommended early termination of the trial. At a median follow-up of 35.1 months (interquartile range, 23.6 to 40.7), a primary-outcome event had occurred in 16 patients in the left bundle-branch pacing group and in 35 patients in the right ventricular pacing group (Kaplan-Meier 4-year cumulative incidence, 8.5% and 19.2%, respectively; hazard ratio, 0.41; 95% confidence interval, 0.23 to 0.75; P = 0.003 by a stratified log-rank test). Serious adverse events unrelated to implantation procedures occurred in 39 patients (11.8%) who had received left bundle-branch pacing and in 33 patients (9.3%) who had received right ventricular pacing (P = 0.32).
sections.conclusion: Among patients with atrioventricular block, left bundle-branch pacing was superior to right ventricular pacing in reducing the risk of a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. (Funded by Project on New Technology of Jiangsu Province and others; OptimPacing ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04624763.).

items.title: Community and EMS Interventions to Improve Survival in Cardiac Arrest.

sections.objective: Early cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and defibrillation improve survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, but evidence from randomized trials about whether community-based implementation strategies improve outcomes is lacking.
sections.methods: We conducted a registry-based, cluster-randomized trial involving adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest treated by emergency medical services (EMS) in North Carolina counties. The counties were grouped into clusters, which were then randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to implement a multifaceted intervention or administer usual care. The intervention included four components: training of 911 telecommunicators to improve rapid recognition of cardiac arrest, training of 911 telecommunicators to improve delivery of CPR instructions from telecommunicators to bystanders, community CPR training, and enhanced use of automated external defibrillators by first responders or bystanders before EMS arrival. Data were collected through the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival. The primary outcome was survival to hospital discharge with a good neurologic outcome (Cerebral Performance Category score of 1 or 2; range, 1 to 5, with higher scores indicating worse neurologic outcome).
sections.results: From July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2026, a total of 28 clusters comprising 11,615 patients were assigned to the intervention group, and 27 clusters comprising 10,844 patients were assigned to the usual-care group. The median age of the patients was 64.0 years, and 36.7% were women. The percentage of patients who survived to hospital discharge with a good neurologic outcome was 9.0% (1048 of 11,608 patients) in the intervention group and 9.4% (1017 of 10,839 patients) in the usual-care group (adjusted odds ratio, 0.97; 95% confidence interval, 0.75 to 1.26; P = 0.80).
sections.conclusion: Among adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, implementation of a multifaceted strategy involving the community and EMS did not result in a greater percentage of patients who survived to hospital discharge with a favorable neurologic outcome than usual care. (Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute of the National Institutes of Health; RACE-CARS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04660526.).

items.title: Retatrutide Once Weekly in Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Obesity.

sections.objective: Retatrutide, an investigational triple agonist of GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptors, may be useful for the treatment of painful knee osteoarthritis in persons with obesity.
sections.methods: In two phase 3 trials, adults without diabetes who had painful knee osteoarthritis and a body-mass index of at least 27 were randomly assigned to receive once-weekly subcutaneous retatrutide (9 or 12 mg in TRIUMPH-4 and 4, 9, or 12 mg in TRIUMPH-1-OA) or placebo. In TRIUMPH-4, the primary end points were the change in the WOMAC pain score (range, 0 to 10, with higher scores indicating worse pain) and the percent change in body weight at week 68. In TRIUMPH-1-OA, the primary end point was the change in the WOMAC pain score at week 80. For non-pain-related end points, intercurrent events were handled with a treatment-policy strategy. For pain-related end points, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy for intercurrent events that suggested treatment failure and a treatment-policy strategy elsewhere. We also report results for an intention-to-treat (ITT) estimand.
sections.results: A total of 445 participants underwent randomization in TRIUMPH-4 and 574 in TRIUMPH-1-OA. At 68 weeks, the mean changes in the WOMAC pain score (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-4 were -3.96 (9 mg) and -3.74 (12 mg), versus -2.12 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -1.83 [95% confidence interval {CI}, -2.37 to -1.30] and -1.61 [95% CI, -2.16 to -1.07], respectively). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -1.70 (95% CI, -2.19 to -1.22) and -1.38 (95% CI, -1.91 to -0.85) (P<0.001 for all comparisons). The mean percent changes in body weight with retatrutide were -20.0% (9 mg) and -23.7% (12 mg), versus -4.6% with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -15.4 percentage points [95% CI, -18.7 to -12.1] and -19.2 percentage points [95% CI, -22.4 to -15.9]; P<0.001 for both comparisons). At 80 weeks, the mean changes in the WOMAC pain score (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-1-OA were -3.22 (4 mg), -3.48 (9 mg), and -3.64 (12 mg), versus -1.87 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -1.35 [95% CI, -1.92 to -0.78], -1.61 [95% CI, -2.20 to -1.02], and -1.77 [95% CI, -2.34 to -1.20], respectively). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -0.96 (95% CI, -1.61 to -0.30), -1.41 (95% CI, -2.07 to -0.75), and -1.64 (95% CI, -2.26 to -1.02) (P≤0.005 for all comparisons). In both trials, serious adverse events were more common with retatrutide than with placebo, and the most common adverse events were gastrointestinal.
sections.conclusion: In participants with painful knee osteoarthritis and obesity, treatment with retatrutide resulted in significantly greater reductions in both the WOMAC pain score and body weight than placebo. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-4 and -1 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05931367 and NCT05929066.).

items.title: Melting and resistivity of iron at Earth core conditions using pulsed Joule heating.
items.abstract: The melting temperature and electrical resistivity of iron at high pressure are essential for understanding Earth's core. Here we use a new high-pressure method - microsecond pulsed Joule heating in diamond anvil cells - to identify melting and measure resistivity of solid and liquid iron. More than 300 reproducible melting measurements indicate a surprisingly shallow melting curve, reaching 6 K/GPa and 4160 ± 80 K at 200 GPa. Extrapolating in pressure and iron alloy composition, and combining with our 76 [Formula: see text] cm measurement of liquid iron's resistivity, we infer a relatively cold core-mantle boundary (3430 K) with a low adiabatic outer core heat flow (9.8 TW). This suggests thermal convection alone could have powered the geodynamo prior to inner core formation and that today's lowermost mantle is fully solid.

items.title: HIV, obesity, and stigma: lessons for programmes, policy, and practice.
items.abstract: HIV has generated four decades of activism, research, and policy reform that produced measurement tools, theoretical frameworks, and consensus that stigma undermines prevention, delays treatment, and entrenches inequity. Weight stigma follows a strikingly similar pattern, operating through visibility, assumptions of personal control, and moralised concern, and is now recognised as a public health priority in its own right. These two forms of stigma increasingly intersect in the same bodies: antiretroviral therapy, particularly newer regimens, is associated with substantial weight gain, so that people once stigmatised for wasting now risk a second, contradictory stigma for excess weight. This intersection is complex; internalised stigma from either condition can resurface long after apparent resolution, even when viral suppression has been reached or after major weight loss. HIV and obesity differ in diagnostic certainty, visibility, permanence, and the origins of activism and legal protection, which helps explain why HIV stigma reduction remains decades ahead. Applying the Health Stigma and Discrimination Framework to this intersection clarifies shared drivers, facilitators, manifestations, and outcomes. Community leadership, rejection of false prevention-versus-treatment trade-offs, equitable access to pharmacotherapy, and integration of obesity care into existing HIV services offer a practical path towards reducing both stigmas.

items.title: Antiretroviral therapy, adiposity, and cardiometabolic risk in people with HIV.
items.abstract: Return to health accounts for only part of the weight gain observed with modern antiretroviral therapy (ART). A fuller account requires integrating recovery from HIV-related catabolism, HIV-associated adipose tissue remodelling, withdrawal of weight-suppressive antiretrovirals, possible direct or permissive effects of newer agents, individual susceptibility, and obesogenic environments. Evidence from ART initiation and switch studies, PrEP trials, and mechanistic research in adipose tissue suggests that ART-associated weight gain is heterogeneous rather than a uniform restorative process. Once adiposity is established, ART switching has a limited ability to reverse weight gain, consistent with the biological persistence of acquired adiposity. Future care should move beyond ART manipulation alone and incorporate early monitoring, body-composition assessment, cardiometabolic prevention, lifestyle intervention, and appropriate antiobesity pharmacotherapy.

items.title: Weight management in people with HIV.
items.abstract: Excess weight gain in people with HIV is now recognised as a common risk associated with the use of guideline-recommended antiretroviral therapy, such that nearly 50% of people with HIV are living with comorbid obesity. Weight gain and clinical obesity exacerbate cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic health complications in this population and chronic weight management strategies that reduce these risks are now an urgent priority. Behavioural interventions can be offered to improve diet and increase physical activity, including increasing protein intake and promoting regular physical activity. Additionally, there is a growing body of evidence to support the use of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapies in people with HIV, along with a historical literature showing the efficacy of tesamorelin; however, there are sparse data to direct the use of other approved obesity management medicines specific to this population. Finally, bariatric surgical interventions are suggested to be safe and efficacious for those with chronic HIV infection and comorbid obesity. This Series paper identifies a range of key evidence gaps and research priorities for obesity management in people with HIV, including a lack of trials of GLP-1 therapies in people with HIV powered to key clinical outcomes, such as major adverse cardiovascular events and body composition endpoints, implementation science to define models of care, and research on the heterogeneities in clinical outcomes of obesity treatment by sex.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of obinutuzumab β in patients with active systemic lupus erythematosus: a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial.

sections.objective: B cells play a central role in the pathogenesis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and are a therapeutic target. We therefore assessed the efficacy and safety of obinutuzumab β, a glycoengineered type II anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, in patients with active SLE.
sections.methods: In this multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial, we enrolled patients who were aged 18-80 years, fulfilled the 2019 European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology-American College of Rheumatology classification criteria for SLE, and had active disease (defined as a Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Disease Activity Index 2000 [SLEDAI-2K] score of 8 or more and positivity for antinuclear antibodies or anti-double stranded DNA antibodies) at 30 tertiary hospitals in China. Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 to receive obinutuzumab β or placebo, stratified by SLEDAI-2K score and 24-h urine protein level. Patients, investigators, and the sponsor were masked to treatment allocation. Patients received intravenous infusions of obinutuzumab β (1000 mg) or placebo on days 1, 15, 169, 183, 365, and 379. All patients maintained their background standard therapy. The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of patients with an SLE Responder Index (SRI)-4 response at week 12 assessed in all patients who were randomly assigned and received at least one dose of study treatment (ie, the full analysis set). Safety was assessed in all patients who received any study treatment and had at least one post-dose safety assessment (ie, the safety analysis set) over 52 weeks. The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05796206) and is complete. People with lived experience were not involved as research partners in this study.
sections.results: Between May 26, 2023, and July 29, 2024, 171 patients were screened for eligibility. Of these, 123 patients were randomly assigned to receive obinutuzumab β (n=61) or placebo (n=62) and were included in both the full analysis set and safety analysis sets. The mean age was 36·1 years (SD 10·3). 115 (93%) of 123 patients were female, eight (7%) were male, and 117 (95%) were Han Chinese ethnicity. At week 12, 32 (52%) of 61 patients in the obinutuzumab β group and 21 (34%) of 62 in the placebo group had an SRI-4 response (adjusted risk difference 19 percentage points, 95% CI 3-36; p=0·022). Serious adverse events occurred in 12 (20%) patients in the obinutuzumab β group and 14 (23%) in the placebo group. One fatal treatment-emergent adverse event (sepsis) occurred in the placebo group.
sections.conclusion: Obinutuzumab β plus standard therapy improved SRI-4 response at week 12 in Chinese patients with active SLE, with a generally manageable safety profile over 52 weeks. These phase 2 findings support further evaluation and longer-term safety follow-up.

items.title: Interleukin-6 Inhibition with Ziltivekimab for Atherosclerotic Disease.

sections.objective: The inflammatory cytokine interleukin-6 is hypothesized to be a therapeutic target for patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease. Whether neutralizing interleukin-6 levels with ziltivekimab, a monoclonal antibody, reduces the risk of adverse cardiovascular events remains unknown.
sections.methods: We conducted a multinational, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving adults with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular inflammation (defined by a high-sensitivity C-reactive protein [CRP] level of ≥2 mg per liter). Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous ziltivekimab (15 mg once monthly) or placebo. The primary efficacy end point was a 3-point major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE). This composite end point included death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke.
sections.results: A total of 6376 patients were included in the full analysis population: 3184 were assigned to receive ziltivekimab and 3192 to receive placebo. The mean age of the patients was 69.4 years, and 27.5% were women. At 24 months, the between-group difference in the median percent change in the levels of inflammatory biomarkers among patients receiving ziltivekimab as compared with those receiving placebo was -76 percentage points for free interleukin-6 and -64 percentage points for high-sensitivity CRP. During a median follow-up of 33 months, a primary end-point event occurred in 561 patients (17.6%) in the ziltivekimab group and in 565 patients (17.7%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.99; 95% confidence interval, 0.88 to 1.11; P = 0.84). Serious adverse events occurred in 54.6% of the patients in the ziltivekimab group and in 54.8% of those in the placebo group; serious infections occurred in 20.4% and 17.9%, respectively.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular inflammation, a strategy of lowering interleukin-6 levels with ziltivekimab did not result in a lower risk of cardiovascular events than placebo. (Funded by Novo Nordisk; ZEUS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05021835.).

items.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Lowering in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes.

sections.objective: Uncertainty persists regarding the effects of intensive blood-pressure lowering in patients with type 2 diabetes.
sections.methods: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in Brazil, patients with elevated blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, and high cardiovascular risk received intensive therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or standard therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure.
sections.results: Of the 9476 ethnically diverse patients who were enrolled, 4745 were assigned to receive intensive therapy and 4731 to receive standard therapy. The mean (±SD) age was 64.7±8.2 years, and 5871 of the patients (62.0%) were women. The mean systolic blood pressure during follow-up (with exclusion of the first 3 months) was 121.8±10.8 mm Hg in the intensive-therapy group and 135.4±8.2 mm Hg in the standard-therapy group. During a median follow-up of 4.0 years (interquartile range, 3.9 to 4.0), a primary-outcome event occurred in 286 patients (6.0%; 1.65 events per 100 person-years) in the intensive-therapy group and in 315 patients (6.7%; 1.83 events per 100 person-years) in the standard-therapy group (hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% confidence interval, 0.77 to 1.06; P = 0.20). Serious adverse events occurred in 706 patients (14.9%) with intensive therapy and in 693 patients (14.6%) with standard therapy.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with type 2 diabetes, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg, as compared with less than 140 mm Hg, did not reduce the occurrence of major cardiovascular events. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-DIABETES ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04040634.).

items.title: Discontinuing Statins in Older Adults without Cardiovascular Disease.

sections.objective: Whether discontinuing statin therapy in older adults with at least two chronic conditions but no known cardiovascular disease affects the time to a first cardiovascular event is not well characterized.
sections.methods: We conducted an international, open-label, randomized, controlled trial that enrolled adults at least 70 years of age who were taking statins for primary prevention. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either discontinue or continue statin therapy and other lipid-lowering therapies. The primary outcome was a composite of nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal ischemic stroke, or death from any cause, whichever occurred first. The primary analysis assessed noninferiority on the basis of the between-group difference in restricted mean event-free survival time at 2 years, with a noninferiority margin of -5.2 weeks.
sections.results: A total of 1880 participants underwent randomization: 938 were assigned to the discontinuation group and 942 to the continuation group. The mean age of the participants was 77.5 years, and 46.9% were women. The between-group difference in the restricted mean event-free survival time at 2 years was -2.0 weeks (95% confidence interval, -3.7 to -0.3; P<0.001 for noninferiority). Over a median follow-up of 103 weeks, 119 participants (12.7%) in the discontinuation group and 87 (9.2%) in the continuation group had a primary-outcome event. At least one serious adverse event occurred in 43.0% of the participants in the discontinuation group and in 39.8% in the continuation group.
sections.conclusion: Among older adults with at least two chronic conditions but no known cardiovascular disease, discontinuation of statin therapy was noninferior to continuation with respect to major cardiovascular events or death from any cause at 2 years. (Funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation; STREAM ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05178420.).

items.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Patients with Previous Ischemic Stroke.

sections.objective: Whether intensive blood-pressure control reduces cardiovascular risk after cerebrovascular events remains uncertain.
sections.methods: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 30 sites in Brazil, we assigned participants with elevated blood pressure and previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack to receive intensive treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or to receive standard treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure.
sections.results: A total of 4368 participants were enrolled, with 2172 assigned to intensive treatment and 2196 to standard treatment. The mean (±SD) age of the participants was 63.9±11.2 years, and 2093 (47.9%) were women. During the follow-up period, excluding the first 3 months, the mean systolic blood pressure was 122.0±11.5 mm Hg (median, 119.6 mm Hg) in the intensive-treatment group and 135.2±9.7 mm Hg (median, 135.0 mm Hg) in the standard-treatment group, with a between-group mean difference of 13.1 mm Hg (95% confidence interval [CI], 12.5 to 13.8). Over a median follow-up of 3.9 years, a primary-outcome event occurred in 236 participants (10.9%; 3.25 events per 100 person-years) with intensive treatment and in 297 (13.5%; 4.11 events per 100 person-years) with standard treatment (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.94; P = 0.007). The composite renal outcome (sustained reduction of ≥50% in the estimated glomerular filtration rate or progression to end-stage renal disease) was more common with intensive treatment. The overall incidence of serious adverse events was similar in the two groups.
sections.conclusion: Among participants with previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg resulted in a lower incidence of major cardiovascular events than targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-STROKE ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04036409.).

items.title: Prehospital Extracorporeal Life Support in Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.

sections.objective: In patients with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) with the use of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation can be performed to establish reperfusion. Data comparing prehospital ECPR with conventional care regarding survival until hospital discharge among patients who are 50 years of age or younger with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest are limited.
sections.methods: In a nationwide, nonrandomized study conducted in the Netherlands, we evaluated the outcomes in young adults who were attended by Helicopter Emergency Medical Services (HEMS) that were equipped to deliver prehospital ECPR (intervention group) as compared with those attended by HEMS without ECPR capability (conventional group). The primary outcome was survival until hospital discharge.
sections.results: A total of 144 patients were included in the intervention group, and 87 were included in the conventional group. In the intervention group, 57 of 144 patients (40%) survived until hospital discharge, as compared with 17 of 87 patients (20%) in the conventional group (odds ratio, 2.72; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.59 to 4.66; P = 0.002). At 6 months, a favorable neurologic outcome was reported in 51 of 141 patients (36%) in the intervention group and in 11 of 85 patients (13%) in the conventional group (odds ratio, 4.22; 95% CI, 2.82 to 6.32). There were 32 adverse events in the intervention group and 11 in the conventional group.
sections.conclusion: Among patients who were 50 years of age or younger with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, incorporating ECPR into HEMS was associated with improved survival until hospital discharge, as compared with conventional care. (Funded by the Dutch Ministry of Health; OnScene ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04620070.).

items.title: Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a).

sections.objective: Pelacarsen, an antisense oligonucleotide, reduces serum levels of lipoprotein(a). However, the effect of pelacarsen on cardiovascular outcomes remains uncertain.
sections.methods: We conducted an international, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving patients with preexisting cardiovascular disease and a lipoprotein(a) level of at least 70 mg per deciliter. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous pelacarsen (80 mg) administered monthly or matching placebo. The primary end point was a major adverse cardiovascular event, defined as a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or urgent coronary revascularization.
sections.results: A total of 8350 patients underwent randomization, with 8322 included in the efficacy analysis; 4157 patients were assigned to receive pelacarsen, and 4165 to receive placebo. The mean age of the patients was 59.7 years, and 27.0% were women. The median lipoprotein(a) level at baseline was 236 nmol per liter. At 12 months, the lipoprotein(a) level was 64.4 nmol per liter in the pelacarsen group and 233.4 nmol per liter in the placebo group. The median follow-up was 4.7 years. A primary end-point event occurred in 511 patients (12.3%) in the pelacarsen group and in 503 (12.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.02, 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.90 to 1.15, P = 0.76). Among patients with a baseline lipoprotein(a) level of at least 90 mg per deciliter, a primary end-point event occurred in 402 of 3266 patients (12.3%) in the pelacarsen group and in 403 of 3274 (12.3%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.87 to 1.15; P = 0.99). Serious adverse events occurred in 1553 of 4166 patients (37.3%) who received pelacarsen and in 1709 of 4154 (41.1%) who received placebo.
sections.conclusion: Pelacarsen did not result in a lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events than placebo at a median follow-up of 4.7 years. (Funded by Novartis; Lp[a]HORIZON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04023552.)See also in NEJM Evidence: Extended Analyses of Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a).

items.title: Cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (DAPT-SHOCK-AMI): a randomised, double-blind trial.

sections.objective: Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) can compromise the administration and absorption of oral P2Y12 inhibitors and carries high ischaemic and mortality risks. This trial assessed whether intravenous cangrelor was non-inferior to crushed oral ticagrelor for short-term clinical outcomes and whether it provided faster and more consistent platelet inhibition in patients with AMI-CS.
sections.methods: DAPT-SHOCK-AMI was a double-blind trial conducted at 29 hospitals across five European countries (Czech Republic, France, Germany, Poland, and Slovakia). Patients older than 18 years with AMI-CS were randomly assigned (1:1 ratio, stratified by centre, age, sex, presence or absence of ST-segment elevation, and mechanical ventilation) to cangrelor (30 μg/kg bolus followed by an infusion of 4 μg/kg per min for at least 2 h) or crushed ticagrelor (180 mg loading dose). The primary laboratory endpoint was a platelet reactivity index of less than 50% at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. The primary clinical endpoint was death, myocardial infarction, or ischaemic stroke at 30 days. The primary clinical endpoint was analysed for non-inferiority with a prespecified margin of 1 percentage point among all randomly assigned patients who received study treatment. The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03551964) and EudraCT (2018-002161-19); recruitment and 1-year follow-up are complete, and 5-year follow-up is ongoing.
sections.results: Between Aug 1, 2018, and Jan 19, 2024, 605 patients (137 [23%] were female) were randomly assigned to cangrelor (n=298) or ticagrelor (n=307); no surviving patients were lost to the 1-year follow-up. The primary laboratory endpoint was analysed in 56 (19%) patients in the cangrelor group and 68 (22%) in the ticagrelor group, and was achieved in 56 (100%) of 56 patients receiving cangrelor and 15 (22%) of 68 receiving ticagrelor (p<0·0001). The 30-day primary clinical endpoint occurred in 112 (38%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 126 (41%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor; non-inferiority was not demonstrated (difference -4 percentage points [90% CI -10 to 3]; Pnon-inferiority=0·13). Major bleeding at 30 days occurred in 19 (6%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 16 (5%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor.
sections.conclusion: To our knowledge, this is the first randomised trial to compare P2Y12 inhibitor strategies specifically in patients with AMI-CS. Cangrelor achieved effective platelet inhibition more frequently than crushed ticagrelor at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. Non-inferiority of cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor was not demonstrated for the primary 30-day clinical endpoint. These trial findings can inform future trials of P2Y12 inhibition strategies in patients with AMI-CS.

items.title: Ruzaltatug rezetecan versus chemotherapy for EGFR-mutated advanced non-small-cell lung cancer progressing after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy (HERON-Lung01): interim analysis of a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China.

sections.objective: Ruzaltatug rezetecan is a novel HER3-directed antibody-drug conjugate that has shown promising antitumour activity and manageable safety in pretreated EGFR-.mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a phase 1 trial. We aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of ruzaltatug rezetecan with chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC that had progressed after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy.
sections.methods: HERON-Lung01 is a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial conducted at 62 sites in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years, with locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC harbouring an EGFR activating mutation (exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation), and had progressed during or after EGFR-TKI therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan 8·0 mg/kg or chemotherapy comprising pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 plus carboplatin (area under the curve 5) or cisplatin 75 mg/m2 for four cycles, followed by maintenance pemetrexed. All treatments were administered intravenously on day 1 of each 3-week cycle. Block randomisation was stratified by presence of brain metastases, EGFR mutation subtype, and use of a first-line third-generation EGFR-TKI. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR), in the intention-to-treat population. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06671379). Recruitment is complete, with the trial ongoing.
sections.results: Between Nov 29, 2024, and Jan 29, 2026, 498 patients were randomly assigned to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan (n=250) or chemotherapy (n=248). The median age was 60·0 years (IQR 54·0-68·0); 276 (55%) patients were female and 222 (45%) male. At the prespecified interim PFS analysis, median follow-up was 7·7 months (95% CI 7·1-8·3). BICR-assessed PFS was significantly longer with ruzaltatug rezetecan than with chemotherapy (median 8·3 months vs 5·4 months; hazard ratio 0·47 [95% CI 0·36-0·60]; one-sided p<0·0001). Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 101 (41%) of 248 patients receiving ruzaltatug rezetecan and 93 (39%) of 239 patients receiving chemotherapy, most commonly decreased neutrophil count (64 [26%] of 248 patients vs 46 [19%] of 239 patients), decreased white blood cell count (29 [12%] vs 29 [12%]), and anaemia (15 [6%] vs 26 [11%]). TRAEs led to treatment discontinuation in three (1%) patients in the ruzaltatug rezetecan group and three (1%) in the chemotherapy group. One death (unknown cause) in the ruzaltatug rezetecan group was considered by the investigator to be possibly treatment related.
sections.conclusion: Ruzaltatug rezetecan significantly prolonged PFS compared with chemotherapy, with a manageable safety profile, in EGFR-TKI-resistant, EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC. These data support ruzaltatug rezetecan as a potential treatment option in this setting.

items.title: Safety and efficacy of the 0/1 h pathway for myocardial infarction in the emergency department: an international, pragmatic, stepped-wedge, cluster-randomised, controlled trial.

sections.objective: The evaluation of patients with suspected myocardial infarction relies on serial measurements of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin. We aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of implementing the guideline-recommended 0/1 h pathway, compared with a 0/3 h pathway, in hospitals that had not yet adopted the newer strategy.
sections.methods: PRESC1SE-MI was an international, pragmatic, stepped-wedge, cluster-randomised, controlled, masked-endpoint trial at 19 hospitals in ten countries. The study included consecutive adults presenting to the emergency department with acute non-traumatic chest discomfort and suspected myocardial infarction. Hospitals using a 0/3 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h) as standard care were randomly allocated to implement the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) after 6 months (early implementation) or 12 months (late implementation). The trial was designed to test the non-inferiority of the 0/1 h pathway for safety and its superiority for efficacy. The non-inferiority margin was set at an odds ratio of 1·3. Analyses were done in the full analysis set. The coprimary safety outcome was a composite of death from any cause or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, and the coprimary efficacy outcome was emergency department length of stay. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05649384, and is active but no longer enrolling.
sections.results: Between Dec 1, 2020, and Dec 31, 2024, 71 983 consecutive patient presentations were screened, of which 67 624 (93·9%) met the eligibility criteria and comprised the full analysis set. Median age was 59 years (IQR 46-73); 29 954 (44·3%) patient presentations were in female patients and 37 670 (55·7%) were in male patients. 13 753 (22·2%) of 62 060 patient presentations with available data were in patients with known coronary artery disease, and 5855 (8·7%) patient presentations had an adjudicated index diagnosis of myocardial infarction. Overall, 36 464 patient presentations were managed with a 0/3 h pathway and 31 160 with the 0/1 h pathway. Death from any cause or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 454 (1·2%) patient presentations in the 0/3 h group and in 341 (1·1%) patient presentations in the 0/1 h group (adjusted odds ratio 0·93 [95% CI 0·77-1·13]; pnon-inferiority=0·0004). The median emergency department length of stay was 309 min (IQR 203-470) in the 0/3 h pathway and 309 min (207-474) in the 0/1 h pathway (ratio of adjusted median times 1·00 [95% CI 0·97-1·02]; two-sided p=0·65).
sections.conclusion: Implementation of the 0/1 h pathway met the prespecified non-inferiority criterion for the 30-day composite safety outcome but did not shorten emergency department length of stay compared with the 0/3 h pathway. In this setting, implementation of the 0/1 h pathway alone should therefore not be expected to improve emergency department throughput.

items.title: Generalised eruptive histiocytosis mimicking lymphoma relapse in a patient with previous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
items.abstract: A 92-year-old man with a history of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma treated with chemoradiotherapy, and later with radiotherapy for an isolated cutaneous relapse with complete response, presented with a 1-month history of multiple asymptomatic erythematous-to-violaceous papules and nodules on the face, trunk, and upper limbs. Given his oncological history and previous skin involvement, lymphoma relapse was the leading diagnostic concern, with cutaneous metastases and sarcoidosis also considered. However, skin biopsies showed a non-Langerhans cell histiocytic infiltrate expressing CD45, CD68, and CD163, without CD1a, CD20, PAX5, S100, or Langerin expression. Skin and blood flow cytometry identified no abnormal cell populations, and a PET-CT scan showed no abnormal metabolic activity. Clinicopathological correlation narrowed the differential to group C (cutaneous) histiocytosis, and subsequent spontaneous regression of the lesions over 3 months without treatment supported the diagnosis of generalised eruptive histiocytosis. At 15 months of follow-up, there was no recurrence or evidence of active disease. This case illustrates that cutaneous histiocytoses can mimic several inflammatory and neoplastic conditions, including lymphoma relapse, reinforcing the need to actively resist cognitive bias in people who have had cancer through reflective reassessment, broad differential diagnosis, and biopsy confirmation.

items.title: Pegcetacoplan for geographic atrophy: Bridging the "clinical relevance gap" through precision medicine.
items.abstract: The approval of pegcetacoplan marks a transformative era in the management of geographic atrophy (GA), offering the first FDA-approved intervention to slow lesion growth. A critical analysis of accumulated data, however, reveals a profound "clinical relevance gap." While pegcetacoplan demonstrates a measurable reduction in GA progression, this anatomical benefit exhibits a striking dissociation from high-acuity visual acuity gains, though emerging data suggests preservation of microperimetric function. We narrative synthesize evidence from pivotal trials, real-world studies, and advanced imaging analyses to interrogate the mechanistic rationale of upstream C3 inhibition, the "CNV Paradox" where therapy exchanges dry atrophy progression for increased exudative conversion, and the risk redistribution inherent in chronic complement blockade. We evaluate the burden of high-frequency intravitreal injections, the implications of rare but devastating inflammatory events like retinal vasculitis, and the limitations of current imaging endpoints. We argue that the therapeutic potential of pegcetacoplan is maximized not by a "treat-all" approach, but through a precision medicine paradigm. Identifying patients with specific biomarkers such as a high ellipsoid zone to retinal pigment epithelium loss ratio bridges the gap between structural preservation and functional relevance, ensuring that the risks of therapy are outweighed by meaningful clinical benefit.

items.title: Statin Use and Age-related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Disease Outcomes.

sections.methods: We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library through October 2025 for randomized trials and cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies with comparators. We assessed risk of bias with tools appropriate to each design and pooled effect measures separately using random-effects models. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO.
sections.results: Twenty-eight studies included 1,918,120 participants. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) for the prevalence of any, early, and late AMD were 1.03 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.86-1.24), 1.10 (95% CI, 0.92-1.31), and 0.75 (95% CI, 0.46-1.25), respectively. For incidence of any AMD, the pooled hazard ratio (HR) was 1.04 (95% CI, 0.82-1.31) and the OR was 0.76 (95% CI, 0.43-1.34), with substantial heterogeneity. For neovascular AMD incidence, different study subsets suggested lower hazard (HR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.60-0.85) and higher risk (risk ratio, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.18-1.44); the OR was inconclusive (0.93; 95% CI, 0.82-1.05). Progression evidence was limited and heterogeneous. Ten of 12 longitudinal nonrandomized studies had serious overall risk of bias.
sections.conclusion: The evidence was of very low certainty and insufficient to establish a protective or harmful effect of statins on AMD. These findings do not support prescribing statins specifically for AMD or discontinuing otherwise indicated therapy.
sections.other: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between statin use and the prevalence, incidence, and progression of age-related macular degeneration (AMD). AMD is a major cause of vision loss in older adults, many of whom receive statins for cardiovascular prevention.

items.title: Fixed Dose Inferior Oblique Recession Has Self-Adjusting Effect.

sections.objective: This study aimed to determine the effect of a uniform dose of unilateral inferior oblique muscle (IO) recession on incomitant hypertropia.
sections.methods: Retrospective consecutive case series. Patients underwent unilateral IO recession by a single surgeon who reinserted the IO 4 mm posterior and 3 mm temporal to the temporal pole of the inferior rectus insertion. Hypertropia was measured in distant central and secondary gazes, and centrally at near. Surgical effects were evaluated by linear regression.
sections.results: Mean patient age was 40±27 (standard deviation) years, and follow-up averaged 448±562 days. Twenty patients had superior oblique palsy. Mean hypertropia in central gaze decreased after IO recession from 8.8±7.9Δ to 1.2±2.9Δ, and in contralateral gaze from 17.0±9.6Δ to 2.1±3.6Δ. Mean preoperative horizontal incomitance decreased after IO recession from 13.7±8.4Δ to 2.4±4.1Δ. Mean vertical incomitance decreased from 6.8Δ to 2.0±4.4Δ. Surgical effect was proportionately greater with greater preoperative hypertropia, resulting on average in nearly ideal correction of all hypertropia at distance in central, ipsilateral, contralateral, as well as in near gazes. This effect generally eliminated incomitance. Three (9%) patients required additional strabismus treatment.
sections.conclusion: Fixed-dose IO recession corrects a wide range of incomitant hypertropia in a self-grading manner, achieving excellent effect for a wide range of hypertropia and incomitance.
sections.other: Thirty-three patients with incomitant hypertropia who underwent identical unilateral IO recession between June 2015 and June 2025. Postoperative hypertropia, incomitance, retreatment, and relationship of initial deviation to surgical effect.

items.title: Amrecibart and cenvacibart for the prevention of catheter-related thrombosis (ROXI-CATH): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial.

sections.objective: Peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) are often complicated by venous thromboembolism, yet no thromboprophylaxis is approved. Factor XI (FXI) inhibition might prevent catheter-associated venous thromboembolism without increasing bleeding. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of amrecibart and cenvacibart for preventing venous thromboembolism after PICC placement.
sections.methods: ROXI-CATH is a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial conducted across 12 hospital centres in Bulgaria, Canada, Israel, Romania, the UK, and the USA. Eligible participants aged 18 years or older undergoing PICC insertion, with the PICC expected to remain for at least 14 days, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 2 or less were randomly assigned (1:1:1) using a permuted block design and stratified by site and diagnosis of active cancer to receive a single intravenous infusion of amrecibart (300 mg; anti-FXI A2 domain monoclonal antibody), cenvacibart (250 mg; anti-FXI catalytic domain monoclonal antibody), or placebo. Participants, principal investigators, and study site staff were masked to treatment assignment. The primary efficacy outcome was adjudicated venous thromboembolism (symptomatic or asymptomatic PICC-associated deep vein thrombosis or superficial vein thrombosis, or pulmonary embolism, including pulmonary embolism-related death) up to day 14. Ultrasounds were performed on days 7 and 14. The key secondary efficacy outcome was adjudicated thrombosis detected by ultrasound in the upper extremity with the PICC up to day 14. The primary safety outcome was site-reported treatment-emergent adverse events up to the end of the study. The key secondary safety outcomes were adjudicated major and clinically relevant non-major (CRNM) bleeding up to day 14. Efficacy analyses were performed in the full analysis set, which consisted of all randomly assigned participants who received any study drug and with any evaluable post-baseline ultrasound or a confirmed episode of venous thromboembolism. Safety analyses were performed in the safety analysis set, which included all randomly assigned participants who received any study drug (as treated). This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06299111 (completed; these analyses were performed after database lock on May 6, 2026).
sections.results: Between Sept 20, 2024, and Dec 19, 2025, 240 participants were screened, and 195 were randomly assigned to amrecibart (n=65), cenvacibart (n=66), or placebo (n=64). One participant in the placebo group who did not receive study treatment and had no evaluable ultrasound was excluded from the full analysis set. The median follow-up time was 100 days (IQR 100-103). The median age was 60 years (49-69), and 89 (46%) of 194 participants were female, 105 (54%) were male, and 192 (99%) were White. Adjudicated venous thromboembolism up to day 14 occured in 13 (20%) of 65 participants in the amrecibart group (odds ratio [OR] 0·37 [90% credible interval 0·18-0·65]), 13 (20%) of 66 participants in the cenvacibart group (0·36 [0·17-0·64]) compared with 27 (43%) of 63 participants in the placebo group. Adjudicated PICC-associated venous thromboembolism up to day 14 occurred in 12 (18%) participants in the amrecibart group (OR 0·30 [95% CI 0·14-0·67]), 13 (20%) participants in the cenvacibart group (0·32 [0·14-0·69]), compared with 27 (43%) participants in the placebo group. Site-reported treatment-emergent adverse events up to day 100 occurred in 45 (69%) participants in the amrecibart group, 42 (64%) participants in the cenvacibart group, and 48 (76%) participants in the placebo group. No participants had major bleeding up to day 14. CRNM bleeding up to day 14 occurred in two (3%) participants in the amrecibart group, two (3%) in the cenvacibart group, and two (3%) in the placebo group. Serious adverse events occurred in nine (14%) participants in the ambrecibart group, six (9%) in the cenvacibart group, and ten (16%) in the placebo group. One (2%) participant in the amrecibart group, four (6%) participants in the cenvacibart group, and two (3%) participants in the placebo group died; these deaths were assessed as not related to treatment by the respective investigators.
sections.conclusion: A single infusion of amrecibart or cenvacibart reduced the incidence of venous thromboembolism following PICC insertion, suggesting FXI inhibition at the A2 or catalytic domain as a promising prophylactic strategy for contact-mediated thrombosis.

items.title: In Vivo CRISPR Base Editing of ANGPTL3 for Durable Lipid Lowering.
items.abstract: Circulating concentrations of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and triglyceride-rich lipoproteins are leading risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease1. Despite several approved lipid-lowering medications, most patients fail to achieve target lipid levels under the chronic care treatment model2,3. Here, we describe a potential single-course treatment in which an infusion of guide RNA and mRNA encoding a CRISPR adenine base editor-encapsulated within a GalNAc-lipid nanoparticle-leads to durable, liver-selective inactivation of angiopoietin-like 3 (ANGPTL3), a known driver of increased LDL-C and triglyceride concentrations. Analyses in human liver cells in vitro confirmed that the base editor introduces a DNA base-pair change at the target ANGPTL3 locus with no detectable off-target editing at any of approximately 3000 candidate sites or treatment-related structural variants. Targeted ANGPTL3 inactivation in nonhuman primates was well-tolerated and led to a > 90% mean reduction in circulating ANGPTL3 protein, with durability confirmed out to 3 years following a single dose. In mouse and nonhuman primate models of hyperlipidemia, gene inactivation was associated with reductions of approximately 40 to 50% in LDL-C and 50 to 70% in triglycerides. These results provided the scientific foundation for initiation of an ongoing first-in-human clinical trial in patients with refractory hyperlipidemia syndromes.

items.title: Single-port Robotic Retroperitoneal Nephroureterectomy with Lower Anterior Access: Surgical Technique, Perioperative and Early Oncological Outcomes from a Multi-institutional Series.

sections.objective: To describe lower anterior access single-port robotic radical nephroureterectomy (LAA-SP RNU), including bladder cuff excision (BCE) and lymph node dissection (LND), without repositioning or redocking.
sections.methods: We present a multicenter retrospective series of 47 patients with upper tract urothelial carcinoma who underwent LAA-SP RNU at five referral centers (May 2024-July 2025). A single 4-cm extraperitoneal incision enabled nephroureterectomy, BCE, and selective hilar/pelvic LND without repositioning or redocking. Data were evaluated using descriptive analyses, and pentafecta achievement for the full cohort was estimated through Kaplan-Meier analysis.
sections.conclusion: LAA-SP RNU appears feasible and associated with acceptable perioperative and early oncological outcomes in experienced centers. Comparative prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed to establish oncological durability, patient benefit, and cost-effectiveness.
sections.other: Median age of the patients was 72 yr; 95% had high-risk disease. LND was performed in 20 patients (43%). Median docking and operative times were 20 and 220 min, respectively; one procedure was converted to open surgery. Grade ≥3 complications occurred in three patients (6%); median hospital stay was 5 d. Pathology showed pT2 and pT3 disease in 15% and 36%, respectively. At median follow-up of 12.3 mo, seven patients (14.9%) experienced recurrence, including five intravesical recurrences; two died from metastatic disease. The 12-mo Kaplan-Meier estimate of pentafecta achievement was 76.7% (95% confidence interval, 62.8-90.5%). This study is limited by potential referral-center and patient-selection bias, heterogeneity in LND and postoperative management, limited follow-up, and the absence of cost-effectiveness data.

items.title: A 3D Deep Learning Model for Assessing Concomitant Pulmonary Embolism Risk by Integrating Clinical and Computed Tomography Venography Features in Patients with Lower Extremity Deep Venous Thrombosis.

sections.objective: The aim of this study was to develop and validate a multimodal deep learning (DL) model integrating clinical and computed tomography venography (CTV) features for predicting concomitant acute pulmonary embolism (PE) risk in patients with lower extremity deep venous thrombosis (LEDVT).
sections.methods: This multicentre retrospective study enrolled patients with LEDVT undergoing both computed tomography pulmonary angiography and lower extremity CTV. Centre 1 data were used for model training and internal validation, while data from centres 2 and 3 were used for external testing. Clinical models (logistic regression [LR], random forest [RF], support vector machine [SVM], and XGBoost), 3D DL models (VGG-11, VGG-16, ResNet-18, Res2Net-50, and DenseNet-121), and combined models (LR, RF, SVM, and XGBoost) integrating clinical, imaging, and DL features were developed to select the best performer, which was further benchmarked against validated clinical risk scores (Wells score and modified Geneva score).
sections.results: A total of 348 patients from centre 1 were randomly split into training and internal validation sets, and 127 patients from two independent institutions formed the external testing cohort. The optimal LR clinical, 3D VGG-16 DL, and SVM combined models achieved external testing area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.776, 0.789, and 0.836, respectively. DeLong tests confirmed that the SVM combined model significantly outperformed the LR clinical model and validated clinical scores (all p < .050) on the external testing set, while yielding a comparable AUC to the 3D VGG-16 DL model. Decision curve analysis indicated higher net benefit for the SVM combined model, alongside superior calibration, and positive net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement values.
sections.conclusion: The SVM combined model integrating clinical, imaging, and DL features demonstrated robust performance, offering a promising tool for predicting concomitant acute PE in patients with LEDVT.

items.title: Efficacy and Safety of Ulinastatin in the Treatment of Patients with Sepsis: The ADJUST Trial.

sections.objective: Urinary trypsin inhibitor (ulinastatin, UTI) has shown potential survival benefits in sepsis; however, conclusive clinical evidence is lacking.
sections.methods: In this multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, adult ICU patients with sepsis meeting Sepsis-3 criteria within 48 hours of admission were randomized (1:1) to receive intravenous UTI (400,000 IU every 8 hours) or placebo, for up to 10 days in addition to standard care. Randomization was stratified by site and septic shock. The primary endpoint was 28-day all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included ICU, hospital, and 90-day mortality, and ICU/hospital length of stay.
sections.results: Of 347 patients randomized, 340 (169 UTI, 171 placebo) received intervention and were included in the safety analysis; after 5 post-intervention withdrawals, 335 (165 UTI, 170 placebo) were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. At 28 days, death had occurred in 39 of 165 patients (23.6%) in the UTI group and in 39 of 170 patients (22.9%) in the placebo group (absolute difference, 0.7% [95% CI -8.4% to 9.7%]; P = .98; hazard ratio 1.03, 95% CI 0.66 to 1.61, P = .90). Secondary outcomes were similar in the two groups. Adverse events occurred in 56.8% (96/169) of UTI and 42.7% (73/171) of placebo patients (absolute difference 14.1%, 95% CI 3.6%-24.6%; P = 0.009).
sections.conclusion: In patients with sepsis, adjunctive UTI did not reduce mortality compared with placebo. Routine use of UTI for sepsis is not supported by these findings.
sections.other: In patients with sepsis, does adjunctive ulinastatin, compared with placebo, reduce 28-day all-cause mortality?

items.title: Eyelid injury and associations with visual outcomes and globe removal after open globe injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Eyelid injury is identifiable at presentation, but its relationship with visual prognosis and globe survival has not been systematically synthesized. This prospectively registered systematic review and meta-analysis (CRD420261441414) evaluated the association between eyelid injury and visual or globe survival outcomes among patients with open globe injury (OGI).MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception through February 21, 2026. Studies reporting visual acuity (VA) or globe survival outcomes stratified by eyelid injury status were included. Eyelid injury encompassed eyelid laceration, lid involvement, eyelid wound, or traumatic involvement as reported by study authors. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-E, and certainty using GRADE. Random-effects models generated pooled odds ratios (ORs), with heterogeneity quantified using I². Twenty-one observational studies were included; 14 contributed to quantitative synthesis. Eyelid injury was associated with higher odds of VA worse than 20/200 (OR, 1.73; 95% CI, 1.20-2.50; p = 0.0036; I²=0.0%), hand motion or worse (OR, 4.99; 95% CI, 2.04-12.21; p = 0.0004; I²=49.7%), no light perception or worse (OR, 3.04; 95% CI, 2.05-4.51; p < 0.0001; I²=0.0%), and globe removal (OR, 4.22; 95% CI, 1.73-10.34; p = 0.0016; I²=53.0%). The association with VA worse than 20/400 was directionally similar but not significant (OR, 1.23; 95% CI, 0.81-1.87; p = 0.3362; I²=0.0%). Low to very-low certainty evidence suggests that eyelid injury is associated with worse visual outcomes and increased odds of globe removal after OGI. Because the pooled estimates are based on crude, unadjusted comparisons, eyelid injury may reflect established markers of injury severity rather than provide independent prognostic information.

items.title: Successful Management of Infective Native Infrarenal Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Associated With Micrococcus luteus and Streptococcus mitis in a 77-year-Old Man.
items.abstract: BackgroundInfected native abdominal aortic aneurysm (INAAA) is a rare but life-threatening condition characterized by rapid progression and high mortality.Case SummaryWe report a 77-year-old male with a history of arterial hypertension, ischemic heart disease, and stage IVB hormone-sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma, presenting with lumbar pain and mild inflammatory activation, including leukocytes 8.8 ×10³/µL and C-reactive protein 3.6 mg/dL (normal <0.50 mg/dL). Computed tomography angiography (CTA) demonstrated a 50-mm infrarenal aneurysm, with periaortic inflammatory changes and a periaortic hematoma. A multidisciplinary decision, made 3 hours after admission, favored urgent open surgical repair with resection and in situ reconstruction. Midline laparotomy with debridement and resection of the affected aorta was performed; in situ reconstruction was carried out using a rifampicin soaked bifurcated Dacron graft covered with bovine pericardium with anastomoses to healthy aortic and iliac segments. Intraoperative cultures identified Micrococcus luteus and Streptococcus mitis, rare pathogens in this context. Targeted therapy included intravenous ceftriaxone during hospitalization, followed by oral amoxicillin-clavulanate and doxycycline for seven weeks. Histopathology confirmed chronic granulomatous abscessed inflammation. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged home on postoperative day 17. At six months, follow-up imaging demonstrated a patent reconstruction without signs of persistent infection.ConclusionThese findings highlight the importance of early recognition, aggressive debridement, and coordinated multidisciplinary management in achieving optimal outcomes in INAAA, particularly when atypical microorganisms complicate diagnosis and therapeutic decision-making.

items.title: Preserved Choroidal Thickness and Vascularity Index in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Report No. 2 from the ORNET Study.
items.abstract: In this prospective ORNET analysis, obstructive sleep apnea was not associated with significant changes in choroidal thickness or vascularity index as measured by optical coherence tomography, suggesting relative preservation of choroidal tissue.

items.title: Neural interface instructs layer 4-appropriate circuit reconstruction with engrafted human brain organoids and improves visually guided behavior.
items.abstract: Repairing precise neural microcircuitry after cortical injury remains a pivotal challenge. Human brain organoids (hBOs) are a promising cell source, but disorganized integration limits their therapeutic potential. Here, we demonstrated that targeted neuromodulation, steered by endogenous narrowband gamma (NBG) rhythms, instructed structural and functional integration of hBO grafts in the injured adult mouse visual cortex. Using a neural interface system, we promoted general graft-host coupling and then delivered NBG-rhythmic stimulation to specific functional clusters. This strategy guided the emergence of layer 4-appropriate molecular and functional properties in grafts, enabled bidirectional connectivity with the host visual circuit, and supported the development of advanced visual processing, including direction selectivity in hBO neurons. Electrophysiologically, graft spiking phase locked to host NBG oscillations. Behaviorally, host visual acuity and contrast sensitivity were significantly restored. Our work established a framework for circuit-level repair, highlighting a synergistic strategy that moves beyond cell replacement to direct the assembly of neural grafts.

items.title: Community health worker-led home blood pressure monitoring in rural sub-Saharan Africa: a diagnostic accuracy study.

sections.objective: Home blood pressure monitoring (HBPM) coordinated by community health workers (CHWs) is a potential strategy to improve hypertension detection in sub-Saharan Africa, yet data on its diagnostic performance in this setting are scarce. We aimed to determine the diagnostic accuracy of CHW-coordinated HBPM in Kenya and The Gambia using daytime ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) as the reference standard.
sections.methods: In this cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study, we recruited a random sample of representative age-stratified individuals aged 30 years or older from the general population of two health and demographic surveillance systems in Kilifi, Kenya, and Kiang West, The Gambia. We used the latest enumeration lists of the two health and demographic surveillance systems as sampling frames and performed computer-generated random sampling within five predefined age strata (30-39 years, 40-49 years, 50-59 years, 60-69 years, and ≥70 years). Pregnant women were excluded, and participants were eligible to participate irrespective of previous hypertension status. CHWs trained and provided participants with HBPM devices for self-measurement of blood pressure twice a day, for a minimum of 3 days and a maximum of 7 days. For the reference standard measurement, an ABPM device was fitted by CHWs, and ambulatory blood pressure was measured every 15 min during the day and 30 min at night. We used blood pressure cutoffs derived from the European Society of Hypertension to determine the age-standardised measures of accuracy (sensitivities, specificities, positive predictive values [PPVs] and negative predictive values [NPVs], positive likelihood ratios [LR+] and negative likelihood ratios [LR-] and area under receiver operating characteristic curves) of HBPM among participants who had valid HBPM and ABPM measurements.
sections.results: Between Aug 18, 2023, and Dec 13, 2024, from 1452 eligible participants, we included 1279 participants with valid HBPM and ABPM measurements (696 in Kenya and 583 in The Gambia). In 1279 participants, the median age was 54 years (IQR 43-66), 805 (62·9%) were women, and 474 (37·1%) were men. The age-standardised prevalence of hypertension on daytime ABPM was 23·1% (95% CI 19·9-26·2) in Kenya and 27·1% (23·6-30·6) in The Gambia while the respective prevalences on HBPM were 32·5% (29·1-35·8) and 31·2% (27·5-34·9). The age-standardised sensitivities and specificities of HBPM were 82·6% (76·2-89·0) and 82·4% (79·0-85·7) in Kenya and 68·7% (61·3-76·1) and 83·5% (79·7-87·2) in The Gambia. The age-standardised PPVs and NPVs were 58·6% (52·0-65·2) and 94·0% (91·6-96·4) in Kenya and 59·9% (52·5-67·2) and 88·1% (84·8-91·4) in The Gambia, respectively. The age-standardised LR+ and LR- were 4·68 (3·67-5·69) and 0·21 (0·13-0·29) in Kenya and 4·15 (3·09-5·21) and 0·37 (0·28-0·46) in The Gambia, respectively. In both countries, the area under receiver operating characteristic curve for HBPM was above 75%.
sections.conclusion: HBPM showed moderate-to-high sensitivity and high specificity for detecting hypertension in two rural sub-Saharan African communities. HBPM represents a promising alternative for increasing hypertension awareness in rural sub-Saharan Africa.

items.title: Thoracic epidural versus paravertebral blockade for reducing chronic post-thoracotomy pain (TOPIC-2): open label, parallel group, superiority, multicentre, randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of paravertebral blockade versus thoracic epidural during the perioperative period in reducing chronic post-thoracotomy pain.
sections.methods: Open label, parallel group, superiority, multicentre, randomised controlled trial. Adult patients undergoing thoracotomy randomised (1:1) to either paravertebral blockade or thoracic epidural using a web based service between January 2019 and September 2023. Participants in the paravertebral group received three single-shot paravertebral injections of local anaesthetic before incision followed by placement of a paravertebral catheter. Participants in the epidural group had a thoracic epidural catheter placed and loaded with local anaesthetic before incision.
sections.results: 770 patients were enrolled, of which 428 (56%) were male (mean (standard deviation, SD) age 66.6 (11.0) years). After 33 exclusions of patients after randomisation who did not proceed to thoracotomy, 737 remained in the modified intention-to-treat population (364 in the paravertebral group, 373 in the epidural group). Six months after randomisation, 59 (22%) of 272 participants in the paravertebral group and 47 (16%) of 292 participants in the epidural group developed chronic post-thoracotomy pain (adjusted risk ratio 1.32 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.93 to 1.86), adjusted risk difference 0.05 (95% CI -0.01 to 0.11), P=0.12). During the acute phase, worst and average pain was greater on day 1 with paravertebral blockade (adjusted mean difference 7.7 mm (95% CI 2.8 to 12.5 mm) and 7.0 mm (95% CI 2.7 to 11.2 mm), respectively), but no different on days 2-3. Hypotension was less common in the paravertebral group than the epidural group (12% v 18%, respectively, adjusted risk ratio 0.66 (95% CI 0.46 to 0.94), adjusted risk difference -0.06 (95% CI -0.11 to -0.01)), as was pruritis (4% v 12%, adjusted risk ratio 0.37 (95% CI 0.21 to 0.64), adjusted risk difference -0.07 (95% CI -0.11 to -0.03)), although more participants in this group experienced urinary retention (12% v 6%, adjusted risk ratio 2.21 (95% CI 1.35 to 3.61), adjusted risk difference 0.05 (95% CI 0.01 to 0.09)), complications were similar otherwise.
sections.conclusion: Paravertebral blockade did not reduce chronic post-thoracotomy pain at six month follow-up compared to thoracic epidural. Thoracic epidural provided marginally better acute pain relief one day after the operation, but showed no difference thereafter. Postoperative complications were comparable between groups. The findings support the ongoing use of both techniques.
sections.other: 15 thoracic centres in the UK.
