sections.conclusion: Poorer hearing was independently associated with thinner middle and inner retinal layers. These findings may suggest shared neural vulnerability across auditory and visual systems, highlighting their potential as indicators of broader neural health.

items.title: Metabolomic Signatures of Healthy Dietary Patterns Associated With Lower Risk of Age-Related Macular Degeneration.

sections.objective: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the association of metabolomic signatures reflecting adherence and metabolic response to dietary patterns with prevalence and structural severity of age-related macular degeneration (AMD).
sections.methods: In this cross-sectional study of 1008 eyes from 504 participants, metabolomic profiles in plasma and urine were measured by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Previously derived signatures for eight dietary patterns-including the Alternate Mediterranean diet (AMED), Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH), plant-based diet indices (PDIs), and two mechanism-based diets including Empirical Dietary Inflammatory Pattern (EDIP) and Empirical Dietary Index for Hyperinsulinemia (EDIH)-were evaluated for association with AMD using linear mixed models and Mendelian randomization (MR).
sections.results: Each signature (38-66 metabolites) correlated with its dietary pattern score (Pearson r = 0.16-0.30). Per SD increase in plasma signatures of four healthy dietary patterns (AMED, DASH, PDI, and healthy PDI [hPDI]) were associated with 12% to 16% lower odds of AMD and reduced severity, whereas the unhealthy PDI (uPDI) signature was associated with 13% higher odds and greater severity (false discovery rate [FDR] < 0.05). DASH showed the strongest inverse association with AMD and with atrophy, hyper-reflective foci, and ellipsoid-zone disruption (β = -0.808 to -0.613). Further MR analyses found that genetically instrumented signatures of DASH and Alternate Health Eating Index (AHEI)-2010 were inversely associated with AMD, whereas the EDIP signature was positively associated.
sections.conclusion: Metabolomic signatures of healthy dietary patterns are associated with lower odds and reduced structural severity of AMD. Further longitudinal studies are warranted to validate these findings.

items.title: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists' National Ophthalmology Database: report 15, severe vision loss following cataract surgery.

sections.objective: To investigate rates of severe vision loss post-cataract surgery.
sections.results: Severe vision loss was recorded in 3723 (0.21%) eyes, including 3 eyes (2 patients) from 2 718 immediate sequential bilateral cataract surgery (ISBCS) eyes. The highest observed SVL rate was 10.68% for eyes recorded as left aphakic after surgery and the second highest observed SVL rate (3.32%) was when posterior capsular rupture occurred. The SVL rate was higher than the overall rate for eyes with previous intravitreal injections (0.76%), eyes with optic nerve or central nervous system problems (0.74%), age-related macular degeneration (0.52%), previous vitrectomy surgery (0.49%), diabetic retinopathy (0.45%), glaucoma (0.42%) or corneal pathology (0.33%). Of 1,642,386 (93.8%) eyes that were not preoperatively legally blind, 2731 (0.2%) were postoperatively legally blind. Of these, 2294 (84.0%) eyes experienced severe vision loss.
sections.conclusion: Severe vision loss from any cause following cataract surgery occurs infrequently. However, it has a higher prevalence in eyes left aphakic, when PCR occurs and for certain ocular comorbidities.
sections.other: Post-cataract severe vision loss (SVL) was defined as a loss of ≥0.60 LogMAR between preoperative presenting visual acuity and postoperative visual acuity. The term 'legally blind' was used for eyes with a corrected visual acuity worse than 1.30 LogMAR. Between 2010 and 2024, there were 1,750,553 eligible operations performed on 1,217,267 patients by 3766 surgeons from 132 centres supplying data to the Royal College of Ophthalmologists National Ophthalmology Database Cataract Audit.

items.title: Making better use of patients' time: feasibility of performing self-administered vision assessments in waiting rooms.

sections.objective: Patients often spend significant time in clinic waiting rooms. This study assessed the feasibility of using this "wasted" time to perform self-administered vision assessments directly within the waiting area.
sections.methods: Glaucoma patients attending routine appointments were asked to complete either a pen-and-paper (SpotChecks) or digital (PopCSF) contrast sensitivity (CS) test. Ambient illuminance, background noise, and crowd levels were recorded to assess potential environmental confounds. Test durations and patient feedback were recorded. Visual-Functioning Index-7 (VF-7) and Pelli-Robson CS (reference) test results were collected for comparison.
sections.results: Of 173 patients approached, 155 (89.6%) agreed to participate, and 151(97.4%) participants completed testing before their appointment (77/78 pen-and-paper; 74/74 digital). Environmental factors had no significant impact (all P > 0.05). Median completion times were 3.0 {2.6-4.5} minutes (pen-and-paper) and 2.5 {2.0-3.5} minutes (digital). Age did not impact the pen-and-paper test duration (P = 0.944) but weakly correlated with the digital test duration (rdigital = 0.27, P = 0.020). Functional CS scores correlated with Pelli-Robson reference measurements (rpen-and-paper = 0.81; rdigital = 0.62), age (rpen-and-paper = -0.58; rdigital = -0.37), logMAR visual acuity (rpen-and-paper = -0.42; rdigital = -0.44), and visual field mean deviation scores (rpen-and-paper = -0.54; rdigital = -0.63). Both tests were highly acceptable to patients ( > 80% on all questions). Visit durations were longer for participants (109 vs 88 min, P = 0.007), but this was attributed to consenting and related research activities rather than the tests themselves.
sections.conclusion: This proof-of-concept study demonstrates that it is feasible for patients to self-administer portable vision tests in clinic waiting rooms. Using CS as a representative example, this approach may enable additional data collection, potentially improving patient management, clinic flow, and/or patient satisfaction.

items.title: Development and External Evaluation of a Clinical Score for High Pretreatment Interferon-γ Release Assay Responses in Psoriasis: A Multicenter Study in China.

sections.objective: The NPF/IPC statement exempts routine tuberculosis (TB) testing for IL-17/IL-23 inhibitors in low-burden settings, but elimination may be unsafe in high-burden regions. To develop and evaluate a clinical score estimating the probability of a high pretreatment interferon-γ release assay (IGRA) response in psoriasis patients before biologic therapy in China.
sections.methods: Adult patients with psoriasis scheduled to initiate biologic therapy who underwent pretreatment screening were retrospectively included from four Chinese hospitals. Logistic regression was used to develop and evaluate the score.
sections.results: The psoriasis TB risk score (PTRS) comprised six items: age>43.0 years (1), BMI>24.8 kg/m2 (2), married status (1), smoking (2), alcohol consumption (3), and acitretin use (-2). The AUC was 0.799 (95% CI, 0.758-0.840) in the development cohort, 0.697 (0.625-0.768) in validation cohort 1, and 0.621 (0.462-0.780) in the exploratory Shenzhen cohort. Positivity rates in the development, validation, and external validation cohorts were 2.4%/8.8%/33.2%, 3.7%/11.8%/20.8%, and 2.9%/8.8%/13.7% for the low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups, respectively.
sections.conclusion: The PTRS stratified the probability of a high pretreatment IGRA response in Chinese cohorts; local validation is required before the score is used to modify testing practice.
sections.other: Retrospective design without longitudinal TB outcomes; performance declined in the geographically distinct cohort.

items.title: External validation of a deep-learning algorithm for perimetric glaucoma detection on color fundus photographs in the Rotterdam Study.

sections.objective: To externally validate a deep-learning (DL) algorithm detecting perimetric glaucoma on color fundus photographs (CFPs) in a population-based cohort.
sections.methods: External validation in a prospective population-based cohort. Participants aged 50-80 years from three Rotterdam Study cohorts. We applied the winning Artificial Intelligence for Robust Glaucoma Screening (AIROGS) challenge algorithm, trained on 101,442 macula-centered CFPs to detect referable presumed perimetric glaucoma. Performance was assessed at eye and participant level, with participant-level cluster bootstrap confidence intervals. Misclassified cases underwent qualitative review. Longitudinal detection was evaluated by Kaplan-Meier analysis. Additionally, paired analyses compared macula- with disc-centered CFPs. A post-hoc analysis examined the effect of image quality on positive predictive value (PPV).
sections.results: Among 19,088 eyes (9,837 participants), 201 eyes (1.1%) had perimetric glaucoma. At eye level, sensitivity at 95% specificity was 70.6% (95% CI: 63.8-76.8), with an ROC-AUC of 0.911 (95% CI: 0.887-0.934) and a PR-AUC of 0.343 (95% CI: 0.274-0.427). At participant level, sensitivity was 68.8% (95% CI: 61.8-75.9) and ROC-AUC 0.909 (95% CI: 0.882-0.934). Overall, this resulted in 5.1 referrals per detected glaucoma case. True positives showed more advanced visual field damage than false negatives (median mean deviation -10.8 vs -5.8 dB; P < 0.001). Among true positives with prior imaging, 33 of 61 (54%) were flagged before conversion, typically 4-7 years before diagnosis. Discrimination in the 90-100% specificity range was higher for disc- than macula-centered CFPs (pAUC 0.860 vs 0.802; P = 0.003). PPV improved substantially after excluding CFPs with incomplete optic nerve head (ONH) visibility.
sections.conclusion: The DL-algorithm achieved meaningful discrimination for perimetric glaucoma in an external population-based dataset. Correctly identified cases were frequently flagged at an earlier examination, years before the perimetric diagnosis. Despite having been trained exclusively on macula-centered CFPs, the DL-algorithm showed no loss of discriminative performance on disc-centered CFPs. Incomplete ONH visibility was an important source of false positives. These findings support CFP-based deep learning as a scalable triage tool for glaucoma screening and highlight image acquisition standards for implementation.
sections.other: Sensitivity at 95% specificity, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), partial AUC (pAUC) for 90-100% specificity, PPV, and precision-recall AUC (PR-AUC).

items.title: Defining the optimal duration of remote home tonometry for accurate characterization of intraocular pressure fluctuation.

sections.objective: To determine the minimal duration of remote intraocular pressure (IOP) monitoring needed to yield accurate IOP fluctuation metrics in patients.
sections.methods: Secondary modeling analysis of retrospective data, validated with a large national database. 397 patients from the Moran Eye Center and/or Wilmer Eye Institute and 1,579 patients from a MyEyes CorporationTM database who utilized an iCare HOME/HOME2 tonometer and recorded ≥3 measurements throughout each day over several consecutive days. Bootstrapped progressive day-censorship analyses and exponential decay modeling were used to estimate the number of monitoring days required to achieve 95% of the maximal model-based reduction in error for IOP metrics, including mean, maximum, range, and standard deviation (SD). Ground truth for each metric was defined using all available measurements within each eye-specific monitoring period. Sensitivity analyses assessing the effects of diagnosis, treatment, and three daily IOP measurements were also completed.
sections.results: Across both datasets, approximately 6-7 monitoring days were required to achieve 95% of the modeled reduction in error for daily mean, maximum, range, and SD of IOP in the primary analysis. Sensitivity analyses demonstrated longer monitoring requirements in primary open-angle glaucoma (9.1-10.0 days) compared with glaucoma suspects (5.5-6.7 days), secondary open-angle glaucoma (6.4-8.0 days), and primary angle-closure glaucoma (7.8-8.3 days). Monitoring durations remained relatively consistent before and after selective laser trabeculoplasty (8.4-9.0 days) and Hydrus microstent implantation (6.0-6.8 days). Restricting measurements to only three daily IOP recordings throughout the day extended monitoring duration to approximately 10 days in the Moran/Wilmer dataset and longer in the MyEyes dataset. Additionally, 74.1% of peak IOP measurements occurred outside typical clinic hours.
sections.conclusion: Remote tonometry provides clinically meaningful characterization of IOP metrics beyond traditional office-based measurements. Depending on the clinical context, seven to ten consecutive monitoring days consisting of measurements across each day are needed to represent a patient's true IOP pattern.
sections.other: Mean absolute error (MAE) and mean relative error (MRE) for IOP mean, maximum, range, and SD; the number of monitoring days required to achieve 95% of the maximal model-based reduction in error.

items.title: Kidney Endpoints in ANCA-Associated Vasculitis - Position Report from the European Vasculitis Society Focus Group Meetings.
items.abstract: Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitides (AAV) often affect the kidneys, driving morbidity and mortality in AAV. Clinical trials have investigated kidney outcomes using a variety of definitions. The standardization of kidney disease response criteria in AAV remains an unmet need, with an urgency to define kidney endpoints for daily clinical practice and new drug development to optimize patient management. A European Vasculitis Society (EUVAS) Focus Group was formed to review the literature and discuss the wide range of definitions used. The group involved nephrologists, pathologists and rheumatologists who met four times over a time frame of two years with the objective of formulating a consensus proposal for standardized kidney endpoint definitions for AAV. The group investigated the terminology and outcome relations of active kidney disease, treatment response and refractory kidney disease, remission and relapse, kidney function recovery and kidney failure requiring kidney replacement therapy. The group reviewed and discussed measurable parameters used for the assessments, such as kidney biopsy, hematuria and proteinuria, serum creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate and novel biomarkers. Here, we report on the current variability in terminology, present an expert proposal for kidney endpoints with a research agenda and outline the future strategy for a Delphi consensus.

items.title: Trends in the burden of diseases and their associations with multidimensional development among children and adolescents in China from 2000 to 2019: a retrospective analysis of a nationwide, repeated, cross-sectional survey.

sections.objective: Rapid social progress has transformed the health profile of Chinese children and adolescents, with declining diseases associated with poverty and rising diseases associated with wealth. This study aims to describe national trends in disease transitions and examine their associations with multidimensional provincial development.
sections.methods: In this retrospective study, we analysed data from the 2000, 2005, 2010, 2014, and 2019 waves of the nationwide, repeated, cross-sectional Chinese National Surveys on Students' Constitution and Health in Han Chinese children and adolescents aged 7-18 years from 30 provinces in mainland China. The survey used a multistage, stratified, cluster-sampling design with balanced distributions by age, sex, and residence (urban vs rural). Collected data were prevalences of diseases associated with wealth and development (overweight and obesity, dental caries, and visual impairment) and their coexistence (multimorbidity associated with wealth) in addition to diseases associated with poverty (undernutrition, anaemia, and Ascaris infestation), and their coexistence (multimorbidity associated with poverty). We integrated 13 provincial indicators reflecting economic, social, environmental, infrastructure, and innovation development to construct a Multidimensional Equality Development Index (MEDI) using an entropy method. To examine national trends in disease transitions and their associations with multidimensional development we used mixed-effects logistic regression and restricted cubic splines. Population-attributable fractions were estimated to describe how development domains related to disease patterns.
sections.results: The study included 1 085 072 participants across five survey waves. Between 2000 and 2019, nationally, the prevalence of diseases associated with wealth increased and that of diseases associated with poverty declined substantially. In 2019, prevalence of visual impairment was highest (67·8%), followed by overweight and obesity (24·3%), dental caries (21·9%), multimorbidity associated with wealth (20·1%), anaemia (10·1%), undernutrition (4·7%), Ascaris infestation (0·8%), and multimorbidity associated with poverty (0·5%). The overall median MEDI score increased from 0·11 (IQR 0·09-0·16) in 2000 to 0·20 (0·15-0·28) in 2019. When data were pooled over 20 years, restricted cubic-spline analyses showed a non-linear association between MEDI score and odds of the disease outcome; higher MEDI scores were generally associated with lower odds of diseases associated with poverty, and higher odds of diseases associated with wealth (excluding visual impairment).
sections.conclusion: Multidimensional development was associated with simultaneous reductions in prevalence of diseases associated with poverty and increases in prevalence of diseases associated with wealth. Disparities in most diseases associated with wealth between higher and lower MEDI areas have largely narrowed, suggesting a potential dual burden in lower MEDI areas and the need for targeted strategies. These findings highlight the need to enhance cross-sector investments to promote balanced, sustainable improvements in child and adolescent health.

items.title: Estimated global treatment costs for 31 cancer types by stage, year, and follow-up period: a systematic review and modelling study.

sections.objective: Cancer is a growing health and economic burden worldwide, yet comprehensive global estimates of cancer treatment costs are sparse. Such data are crucial for economic evaluations to inform policy making and practice to improve cancer control and outcomes. We aimed to synthesise available estimates of direct cancer treatment costs by stage, year, and follow-up period and predict global cancer treatment costs.
sections.methods: In this systematic review and modelling study, we extracted estimates of cancer treatment costs (ie, direct treatment costs only) from the medical literature, screening 25 896 studies, of which 196 were included in our final dataset, covering 31 cancer types across 44 countries. Costs were standardised as a ratio of country GDP per capita and adjusted for follow-up period. We used a Bayesian hierarchical model to synthesise the estimates as a function of GDP per capita, accounting for cancer type, stage (I-IV), year of diagnosis, and follow-up period. We then estimated global and regional treatment costs (overall and by cancer type) in US$ 2022 based on the latest available incidence data from GLOBOCAN. This study is registered on PROSPERO (#CRD420251138446).
sections.results: Globally, total 10-year treatment costs for newly diagnosed cancers in 2022 were estimated to be $771·48 billion (95% UI 719·99-823·81), with breast cancer being the largest driver of costs ($96·07 billion [80·78-109·43]), followed by leukaemia ($86·11 billion [80·36-94·87]) and lung cancer ($84·36 billion [73·18-95·28]). North America and Europe accounted for 64% of total costs, but only 36% of diagnosed cancer cases. Mean costs per diagnosed patient were $38 650 (95% UI 36 070-41 280) globally, ranging from $3380 (95% UI 2960-3820) in eastern Africa to $93 600 (95% UI 87 170-100 150) in North America. As a ratio of GDP per capita, treatment costs declined with increasing GDP per capita (from 3·16 [95% UI 2·61-3·81] at $500 GDP per capita to 1·36 [1·07-1·70] at $100 000 GDP per capita), especially for stage IV cancers, which declined from 8·06 (6·57-9·61) at $500 GDP per capita to 4·53 (3·48-5·83) at $100 000 GDP per capita. Cancer types with the highest mean cost ratios were bone cancer (6·27 [95% UI 2·45-11·73]), leukaemia (6·16 [5·59-7·01]), and multiple myeloma (5·74 [3·78-6·74]). Treatment costs remained stable over time by year of diagnosis for stage I-II cancers, but steadily increased for stage III cancers, and rose substantially for stage IV cancers.
sections.conclusion: These cost estimates provide new important data for economic evaluations, which can support expenditure planning, priority setting, and policy making to help guide strategic investment and resource allocations to improve cancer care and outcomes across different settings.

items.title: Effect of ethnicity on response to treatment escalation in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus from the British Isles Lupus Assessment Group Biologics Register (BILAG-BR): a longitudinal cohort study.

sections.objective: Ethnic disparities in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) outcomes are well documented, but data on treatment response across ethnic groups remain scarce. We aimed to evaluate the effect of ethnicity on clinical outcomes following treatment escalation in a diverse UK cohort.
sections.methods: In this longitudinal cohort study, we analysed data from the British Isles Lupus Assessment Group Biologics Register (BILAG-BR), including patients recruited from 64 UK secondary and tertiary rheumatology and nephrology centres. Eligible patients were aged 16 years and older, with active moderate-to-severe SLE, defined as having at least one BILAG A score, at least two BILAG B scores, or a SLEDAI-2K score of at least 6, who had initiated rituximab or belimumab within the past 12 months, or standard immunosuppressive therapy within the past 1 month. Ethnicity was categorised as White, South Asian, Black, East Asian, or mixed or other ethnicities. The primary outcome was major clinical response (MCR) at 6 months and 12 months, measured using mixed-effects logistic regression. Individuals with lived experience of SLE were involved in the study design.
sections.results: Between July 1, 2010, and Nov 10, 2021, 1688 patients were recruited to the BILAG-BR. Of these, 1266 were excluded because they did not meet the study eligibility criteria, and 422 patients were included in the study. 383 (91%) patients were female, 39 (9%) were male, and the median age was 40·5 years (IQR 31·3-50·8). 245 (58%) of 422 patients were White, 77 (18%) were South Asian, 70 (17%) were Black, 19 (5%) were East Asian, and 11 (3%) were of mixed or other ethnicities. At baseline, Black patients had higher baseline disease activity, greater organ damage, and more comorbidities. At 12 months, 99 (23%) of 422 patients had met MCR criteria, including eight (42%) of 19 East Asian patients, 23 (30%) of 77 South Asian patients, 60 (24%) of 245 White patients, seven (10%) of 70 Black patients, and one (9%) of 11 patients with mixed or other ethnicities. In the adjusted five-group model, patients of Black ethnicity had lower odds (OR 0·13 [95% CI 0·02-0·88]) of meeting MCR criteria compared with White patients.
sections.conclusion: MCR criteria were met by fewer than a quarter of patients after treatment escalation. Patients of Black ethnicity had higher baseline disease burden and lower observed response than White patients. These results support the need for more personalised, equitable approaches to SLE management and reinforce the importance of ensuring diversity in clinical research.

items.title: Coronary CT Angiography versus Intravascular Ultrasound Guidance for PCI.

sections.objective: Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes. Coronary computed tomographic angiography (CCTA) provides anatomical and physiological information before cardiac catheterization that may enable PCI planning. Data regarding the use of CCTA-guided PCI as compared with IVUS-guided PCI with respect to clinical outcomes are lacking.
sections.methods: In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, noninferiority trial with blinded end-point adjudication, we randomly assigned patients with a clinical indication for revascularization, at least one epicardial lesion with a diameter stenosis of more than 70%, and a fractional flow reserve derived from CCTA of 0.80 or less in a 1:1 ratio to a CCTA-guided or IVUS-guided PCI strategy. The primary end point was target-vessel failure, defined as a composite of death from cardiac causes, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization, at 12 months. The noninferiority margin for the absolute risk difference was 4.5 percentage points, with a prespecified hierarchical testing strategy for superiority.
sections.results: A total of 1105 patients underwent randomization: 556 to the CCTA-guided PCI group and 549 to the IVUS-guided PCI group. The median age of the patients was 65 years, and 21.7% were women. At 12 months, target-vessel failure had occurred in 23 patients (4.1%) in the CCTA-guided PCI group and in 25 patients (4.6%) in the IVUS-guided PCI group (risk difference, -0.42 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -2.82 to 1.99; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.73 for superiority). A total of 6 patients in the CCTA-guided PCI group and 9 patients in the IVUS-guided PCI group had clinical procedural complications.
sections.conclusion: A CCTA-guided PCI strategy was noninferior to IVUS-guided PCI with respect to target-vessel failure at 12 months. (Funded by GE HealthCare and Heartflow; P4 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05253677.).

items.title: Bilateral Iliac Branch Endoprosthesis Deployment With IVUS-Guided Contrast-Sparing Technique: A Complex Case Report.

sections.objective: Preserving internal iliac artery (IIA) patency during endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) for aortobiiliac aneurysms typically requires substantial contrast volume, posing risk to patients with renal insufficiency.
sections.conclusion: Intravascular ultrasound-guided bilateral IBE is feasible and substantially reduces contrast exposure in patients with renal impairment, though technical flexibility is essential for complex anatomy.Clinical ImpactIVUS-guided bilateral iliac branch endoprosthesis deployment may offer a contrast-sparing option for patients with chronic kidney disease undergoing endovascular repair of complex aortobiiliac aneurysms. Using IVUS for vessel identification, sizing, landing-zone selection, and stent-apposition assessment can reduce reliance on iodinated contrast while preserving internal iliac artery perfusion. This case shows that bilateral reconstruction is feasible with only 38 mL of contrast, even when complex anatomy requires axillary access. Its innovation is using IVUS as the primary guidance modality, with angiography reserved for confirmation and troubleshooting.
sections.other: We present the case of an elderly female with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3b (baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate 35 mL/min/1.73 m², serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL) and an aortobiiliac aneurysm who underwent complex bilateral iliac side-branch (iliac branch endoprosthesis [IBE]) deployment. The procedure used intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) as the primary guidance to minimize contrast exposure. A notable intraoperative challenge arose on the left side, where retrograde cannulation was unsuccessful due to anatomical tortuosity and sheath dislodgement. We therefore performed a left axillary cut-down, which facilitated successful IIA reconstruction and resolved a type 1b endoleak. The total contrast volume employed was approximately 38 mL. Incidental findings included hyperthyroidism and suspected lymphoproliferative disorder.

items.title: Reframing the manosphere: a public health response to a commercial ecosystem.
items.abstract: The manosphere, a diffuse commercial ecosystem and loose collection of online communities united by shared beliefs about masculinity, misogyny, and male victimisation, is an under-recognised determinant of health harms. This network has been implicated in considerable health harms: widespread mental health impacts, especially in young people; violence against women, girls, and gender minorities; and delegitimising help-seeking in boys and men. In this Viewpoint, we argue that the manosphere is best understood and addressed as a public health problem.

items.title: Charting a course to men's health and wellbeing: applying a lens of power and politics to improve men's health outcomes.
items.abstract: Despite long-standing evidence of poor health and life expectancy outcomes among men, particularly among men who are socially or structurally marginalised, men's health has generally received little and uneven attention in health policy and practice. Its gendered and intersectional aspects have been especially overlooked. This third paper in the Lancet Men's Health Series examines why men's health has received so little policy attention and proposes strategies to raise men's health on national and global agendas. We applied a gender lens to the 3-i theory-based framework and analysed how ideas, interests, and institutions shape the prioritisation of men's health within national and global policy agendas. We review the modest development of men's health policies and assess how power and politics, including the roles of a range of stakeholders from global and national health spaces, commercial actors, and civil society organisations, have shaped the construction of the problem as well as policy attention and framing, resource allocation, and interventions. The scarcity of attention paid to men's health on global and national agendas reflects how power operates through ideas and institutions which contribute to the conflation of gender with women, institutional inertia, and contested constructions of individual versus structural drivers of ill health. We highlight how this has created a space in which commercial actors, including the manosphere, can shape narratives and influence men's health in ways that align with commercial or ideological interests. We conclude by proposing politically informed strategies that recognise how power, institutional arrangements, and competing interests shape men's health policy within prevailing gender and structural orders. We identify entry points for advancing men's health equity and wellbeing that draw on empirical evidence and technical guidance, are grounded in political realities, and are consistent with a commitment to gender justice for all people.

items.title: A global men's health epidemiology within an intersectional framework.
items.abstract: Males have lower life expectancies and greater disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) than females, and particularly poor outcomes are seen among males in marginalised contexts. In this paper, we provide an epidemiological overview and highlight the intersectional nature of men's health. We analyse mortality and DALYs data from the 1990-2023 Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Studies to illustrate our intersectional framework and draw attention to how health varies in men and to show key themes. Conditions that contribute most to the poor health of males include non-communicable diseases (eg, cardiovascular diseases and cancers), substance use, suicide, injuries (eg, road traffic incidents and interpersonal violence), and respiratory infections (eg, tuberculosis and COVID-19). Although cardiovascular disease and cancer make the largest contributions to men's higher mortality rates, determinants of health such as violence and war, migration, economic stagnation, and labour market changes due to automation and new technologies will disproportionally affect their health in the future. Injuries, violence, and other external morbidity causes often occur at a young age and in unequal distributions across the sexes, making a large contribution to DALYs. Although biology plays a role, the pattern of many diseases contributing to health differences reflects the intersection of health behaviours, shaped by patriarchy, ideas of masculinity, and structural drivers (including commercial determinants of health); many of these are preventable. Although improvements in some health behaviours are seen, exceptions occur in marginalising social conditions (eg, incarcerated men, men experiencing homelessness, men with mental illnesses, men with substance use disorders, men with low income, men who have sex with men, and those who are gender non-conforming). Multiple data sources detail men's shorter life expectancies and the drivers compared with women, but going beyond sex disaggregation remains challenging and is an urgent priority for research and health monitoring.

items.title: Men's health: an intersectional and multilevel framework for understanding syndemic patterns of health.
items.abstract: Men occupy a privileged position within gender power relations: the male body has been the default reference point for biomedical research and therapeutic development (with the historical exclusion of women from medical trials), and men dominate health services leadership and exercise well documented medical misogyny. Yet despite their privileged position, many aspects of men's health outcomes are neglected and undertheorised because they are not examined through an intersectional gender lens. Although consideration of gender and masculinity is important for understanding men's health, research thus far has focused predominantly on men's harmful health behaviours, overemphasising individual determinants of health, and a deficit-based approach. Little attention has been paid to the influence of structural determinants of men's health risks and vulnerabilities, or the gender-specific health outcomes of worsening social and economic inequalities. In this first paper of a Lancet Series on men's health, we present a conceptual framework for understanding men's health from an intersectional perspective, highlighting how structural, social, and commercial determinants of health, intersectionality, and syndemic theory can be combined to analyse men's health at different socioecological levels. We illustrate the framework using four selected case studies that show how the health outcomes of marginalised men are influenced by complex interactions. We provide a working definition of men's health that reflects existing literature and builds on the conceptual framework and case studies. Promotion of gender justice and health equity requires moving beyond one-dimensional approaches that construct men as problematic individuals, and towards better understanding and action on the broader set of power systems and structural determinants underpinning men's health.

items.title: Non-invasive tests in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: the LITMUS prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study.

sections.objective: The advent of regulatory-approved pharmacological treatments for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) calls for precise, non-invasive biomarkers that facilitate early diagnosis, support therapy selection, and aid clinical trial enrolment. The European multicentre LITMUS study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of a broad range of non-invasive biomarkers for identifying patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), at-risk MASH, advanced fibrosis, and cirrhosis.
sections.methods: In this prospective, multicentre, diagnostic accuracy study, adults with biopsy-confirmed MASLD were prospectively recruited across 13 countries in Europe and the USA. We assessed 12 single markers and 18 multimarker panels. The reference standard was centrally scored liver histology according to the non-alcoholic steatohepatitis Clinical Research Network Scoring System. Target conditions included MASH (Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Activity Score ≥4 with ≥1 point per component), at-risk MASH (MASH plus significant fibrosis [fibrosis stage F≥2]), advanced fibrosis (F≥3), and cirrhosis (F4). Performance was evaluated by area-under-the-receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with the minimum acceptable criterion (MAC) of AUC higher than 0·80 to indicate potential biopsy replacement.
sections.results: Between Jan 1, 2018, and June 30, 2023, we analysed data from 1590 participants with centrally scored liver biopsies and at least one biomarker measurement; 609 (38%) had biopsy-confirmed at-risk MASH, 678 (43%) had MASH, 585 (37%) had advanced fibrosis, and 164 (10%) had cirrhosis. For detecting at-risk MASH, SomaSignal showed the highest diagnostic performance (AUC 0·83 [95% CI 0·80-0·85]), significantly exceeding MAC, whereas no other test reached the MAC for MASH only. For advanced fibrosis, SomaSignal showed the highest performance (AUC 0·92 [0·90-0·94]), followed by FibroMeter-VCTE (AUC 0·87 [0·83-0·92]), Agile 3+ and TSP2 (both AUC 0·84 [0·82-0·86]), and NIS4 (0·82 [0·80-0·85]). For cirrhosis, FibroMeter-VCTE showed the highest diagnostic performance (AUC 0·94 [0·90-0·97]) followed by SomaSignal (AUC 0·92 [0·90-0·94]), followed by Agile 3+ (0·88 [0·85-0·91]), Agile 4 (0·87 [0·84-0·90]), ADAPT (0·85 [0·81-0·88]), and ELF, LSM-VCTE, and TSP2 (all 0·84 [0·81-0·87]). Sequential two-step approaches using gamma-glutamyl transferase as a first-line test met the MAC for both advanced fibrosis and at-risk MASH.
sections.conclusion: Although single markers resulted in variable and limited performance when compared to histology for detecting at-risk MASH, multimarker panels showed great potential, with a proteomic panel showing strong diagnostic performance. These findings could support the selection and implementation of non-invasive testing strategies in MASLD and inform future clinical guidelines, regulatory evaluation, and clinical trial design.

items.title: Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSpect): an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: Data on prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV) used separately or in combination in patients with paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS) are inconclusive, leading to wide practice variability. We aimed to compare the effects of prone positioning with supine positioning and the effects of HFOV with conventional mechanical ventilation on ventilator-free days in children with early, moderate-to-severe PARDS.
sections.methods: PROSpect was an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial done in 75 paediatric intensive care units in 18 countries. Eligible patients were aged 2 weeks to 20 years, and were intubated and mechanically ventilated for less than 96 h before meeting criteria for moderate-to-severe PARDS. Patients were centrally randomly assigned using a web-based system to supine positioning and conventional mechanical ventilation, prone positioning and conventional mechanical ventilation, supine positioning and HFOV, or prone positioning and HFOV. Initially, the allocation was 1:1:1:1 stratified by age group and direct or indirect lung injury using a permuted block design with blocks of four and eight. Response-adaptive randomisation updates were planned to adjust allocation probabilities 28 days after 300 patients were randomly assigned and then 28 days after every 100 additional patients. Given the nature of the interventions, masking was not possible. The primary outcome was ventilator-free days through to day 28 among all randomly assigned participants. Safety was assessed prospectively by daily monitoring for the occurrence of prespecified adverse events. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03896763) and is closed to enrolment.
sections.results: Between May 1, 2019 and Jan 13, 2026, 1045 patients were eligible for enrolment. The trial was stopped early for futility and slow enrolment after 424 of 600 planned patients were recruited. 126 patients were randomly assigned to the supine and conventional mechanical ventilation group, 130 to the prone and conventional mechanical ventilation group, 90 to the supine and HFOV group, and 78 to the prone and HFOV group. Median age was 3·3 years (IQR 1·1-10·1), 211 (50%) patients were female, and 213 (50%) were male. There were no significant differences in ventilator-free days between prone and supine positioning (median 17·9 days [IQR 8·9-21·3] vs 17·4 days [6·4-21·9]; Hodges-Lehmann location shift adjusting for ventilation 0·0 [95% CI -0·8 to 1·0]) or between HFOV and conventional mechanical ventilation (17·3 [5·7-21·6] vs 18·0 [9·9-21·5]; Hodges-Lehmann location shift adjusting for positioning -0·3 [95% CI -1·5 to 0·5]). 41 (10%) patients had died at day 28, without group differences. Plugging or obstruction of the artificial airway occurred more frequently with prone than supine positioning (14 events in 12 [6%] of 188 patients vs three events in three [2%] of 197 patients; 0·74 [95% CI 0·44-1·26] vs 0·15 [0·05-0·47] events per 100 artificial airway days; rate ratio 4·83 [95% CI 1·38-16·82]). Stage 2 or worse immobility-related pressure injuries also occurred more frequently with prone versus supine positioning (12 [6%] vs two [1%]; relative risk 6·13 [95% CI 1·45-25·97]). Haemodynamic instability occurred more frequently with HFOV than conventional mechanical ventilation (41 events in 19 [13%] of 141 patients vs 38 events in 22 [9%] of 244 patients; 2·21 [95% CI 1·63-3·00] vs 1·22 [0·89-1·68] events per 100 paediatric intensive care unit days; rate ratio 1·84 [95% CI 1·18-2·87]). One serious adverse event, an unwitnessed self-extubation followed by cardiopulmonary arrest, occurred in a patient in the prone and conventional mechanical ventilation group.
sections.conclusion: We found no evidence to support prone positioning or HFOV as first-line strategies to improve ventilator-free days in patients with early, moderate-to-severe PARDS. Thus, the routine use of these strategies in this population is not recommended.

items.title: Endometrial ablation plus levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system versus endometrial ablation alone in women with heavy menstrual bleeding in The Netherlands (MIRA2): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.

sections.objective: Endometrial ablation is an established and effective treatment for women with heavy menstrual bleeding, but many patients require further treatment, with approximately 10% ultimately undergoing a hysterectomy within 2 years. The insertion of a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) immediately after endometrial ablation might inactivate residual untreated endometrium or prevent its regeneration, thereby preventing recurrent symptoms necessitating a hysterectomy. The aim of the study was to assess whether LNG-IUS insertion immediately after endometrial ablation in women with heavy menstrual bleeding reduced the need for subsequent hysterectomy within 2 years compared with endometrial ablation alone.
sections.methods: This multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 34 hospitals in the Netherlands. Women younger than 60 years with heavy menstrual bleeding who were eligible for endometrial ablation were included and randomly assigned (1:1) to combined treatment comprising endometrial ablation plus LNG-IUS or to standard care comprising endometrial ablation alone (stratified by dysmenorrhoea and age). Masking was not applied. Endometrial ablation was done using electrical radiofrequency ablation or by transcervical resection of the endometrium. In participants allocated to combined treatment, intrauterine insertion of an LNG-IUS containing a total of 52 mg of levonorgestrel (releasing 20 μg per day in the first year) was done immediately after the ablative procedure. The primary outcome was the incidence of hysterectomy within 2 years, analysed on a modified intention-to-treat basis in all participants with available data. Serious adverse events were systematically assessed at 6 weeks, 12 months, and 24 months after the intervention. This study was registered on the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (NL-OMON54839) and is complete.
sections.results: Between Nov 19, 2019, and April 5, 2023, 715 participants were randomly assigned to combined treatment (n=359) or endometrial ablation alone (n=356). The median age of all participants was 45 years (IQR 40-48). 42 (6%) participants had missing data for the primary outcome at 2 years of follow-up. A hysterectomy was done in 15 (4%) of 342 participants in the combined treatment group versus 34 (10%) of 331 participants in the endometrial ablation group, corresponding to a relative risk (RR) of 0·43 (95% CI 0·24 to 0·77; p=0·0050), with a risk difference of -0·06 (95% CI -0·10 to -0·02; p=0·0040). Serious adverse events were reported in 27 (8%) of 346 participants in the combined treatment group and 26 (8%) of 327 participants in the endometrial ablation alone group (RR 0·98, 95% CI 0·59-1·65; p=0·94), and there were no treatment-related deaths.
sections.conclusion: The combination of endometrial ablation and LNG-IUS significantly reduced the incidence of hysterectomy compared with endometrial ablation alone. The combined treatment appears to be a safe adjunctive strategy for heavy menstrual bleeding that does not increase the risk of complications.

items.title: Disease-free survival and overall survival after neoadjuvant immunotherapy in mismatch repair-deficient colon cancer in the Netherlands: results of the single-arm, multicentre, phase 2, NICHE-2 trial.

sections.objective: Neoadjuvant immune checkpoint blockade induces high pathological response rates in patients with locally advanced mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) colon cancer, yet long-term survival outcomes have not been established. Previously, we reported safety (a primary endpoint) and pathological response (a secondary endpoint) data from the NICHE-2 trial. Here, we report the primary efficacy endpoint of 3-year disease-free survival and the exploratory endpoint of 5-year overall survival.
sections.methods: In this single-arm, multicentre, phase 2, NICHE-2 trial, patients with previously untreated, clinical stage 2 or 3, resectable dMMR colon cancer received a single dose of intravenous ipilimumab (1 mg per kg) on day 1, and two doses of intravenous nivolumab (3 mg per kg) on days 1 and 15, followed by surgery in one of the six participating hospitals in the Netherlands. Here, we report the independent primary efficacy endpoint of 3-year disease-free survival (time from surgery until disease recurrence or death from any cause) and the secondary endpoint of circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) analysis. Overall survival (time from study enrolment until death from any cause) is reported as an exploratory post-hoc analysis. All endpoints were assessed in the per-protocol population (patients who met the eligibility criteria and received at least one cycle of therapy). The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03026140, and has completed accrual.
sections.results: From July 4, 2017, to July 18, 2022, 123 patients were screened, of whom 115 were treated and 111 were included in the per-protocol population. At the data cutoff (June 19, 2026), the postoperative median follow-up was 58·7 months (IQR 49·0-72·9). The 3-year disease-free survival was 100% (97·5% CI 100-100). After a median follow-up of 60·4 months (IQR 50·6-74·1), calculated from time of study enrolment, the 5-year overall survival was 100% (95% CI 100-100). In patients with available plasma samples, ctDNA was detected in 99 (92%) of 108 patients at baseline, and ctDNA clearance was observed in 44 (45%) of 98 patients after the first cycle in week 2 and in 80 (82%) of 97 patients after the second cycle before surgery. In patients with a pathological near-complete response and complete response, presurgery ctDNA clearance was observed in 19 (70%) of 27 patients and 60 (92%) of 65 patients, respectively. Assessment for minimal residual disease after surgery revealed that all patients were ctDNA negative.
sections.conclusion: In patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer, treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab before surgery resulted in a 3-year disease-free survival and 5-year overall survival of 100%. These findings support neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab as a potential standard of care for patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer.

items.title: An explainable artificial intelligence system for prognostic assessment and decision support in diabetic foot ulcer care: a multicentre derivation and validation study with prospective randomised evaluation.

sections.objective: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) carry risks of recurrence, amputation, and all-cause mortality, but most prediction models address single outcomes and have limited interpretability. We developed an interpretable multi-outcome machine-learning framework for individualised DFU risk assessment and prospective clinical evaluation.
sections.methods: We conducted a development and validation study across three hospitals in China from January 1, 2018, to April 30, 2025. We used electronic medical records and follow-up data from 763 patients at Centres A and B to develop and internally validate an ensemble of single-task extreme gradient boosting (ST-XGBoost) and single-task multilayer perceptron (ST-MLP) models to predict cure, recurrence, amputation, and all-cause mortality. The locked ensemble was externally validated in 100 patients at Centre C. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis, with interpretability evaluated using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). From January 5 to March 5, 2026, we performed a prospective comparative evaluation. We randomised 202 participants (1:1) to usual care or artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted care, of whom 200 were analysed. We compared AI-assisted physician decision-making via an evolvable web-based online prediction platform versus usual care. The outcome was overall quality score of the final clinical recommendation. The platform supports follow-up data collection for future offline model updating.
sections.results: In the training dataset, cure, recurrence, amputation, and all-cause mortality occurred in 638, 208, 226, and 167 patients, respectively; the corresponding numbers in the external validation dataset were 80, 34, 24, and 25. In independent external validation, the ST-XGBoost + ST-MLP ensemble outperformed six comparators, with a macro-averaged AUC of 0.901, accuracy of 0.875, and F1 score of 0.830. Outcome-specific discrimination was highest for amputation (AUC 0.953) and all-cause mortality (AUC 0.951), followed by cure (AUC 0.880) and recurrence (AUC 0.820). In the prospective evaluation, AI-assisted recommendations received higher scores than corresponding clinician recommendations (7.77 vs 6.47; mean difference 1.30, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.08-1.52; p < 0.0001), with the largest gain in completeness. The AI-assisted group showed better short-term follow-up engagement and glucose-management adherence.
sections.conclusion: We demonstrate that integrating gradient-boosted trees and neural networks enables explainable prediction of complex DFU trajectories and may support prioritised, individualised clinical decision-making. Nevertheless, recurrence estimates should be interpreted cautiously.

items.title: Age-dependent structural evolution of a functional amyloid contributes to memory impairment in Drosophila.
items.abstract: Cryogenic electron microscopy has revealed endpoint structures of ex vivo amyloid filaments, but how amyloids assemble and evolve in living organisms-and how these transitions affect physiology-remains poorly understood. Here, we map the age-dependent structural landscape of Orb2 amyloid, a synaptic translation regulator required for long-term memory, across the adult lifespan of Drosophila melanogaster. By determining multiple Orb2 amyloid structures, we uncover a dynamic, age-linked progression of amyloid states. Translation-promoting assemblies predominate early in life, whereas aging shifts the Orb2 amyloid ensemble toward structurally distinct, destabilization-resistant assemblies with reduced translational activity, coinciding with memory impairment. Manipulating memory-related chaperones in the brain shifts Orb2 toward youthful, translation-promoting states and improves memory in old flies; conversely, shifting Orb2 toward aged-like, translation-deficient states in young adults is associated with premature memory impairment. These findings define an in vivo trajectory of amyloid evolution and link amyloid structural dynamics to synaptic translation and memory.

items.title: Acute-on-chronic liver failure: A global multisociety consensus on definitions.
items.abstract: The acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) multisociety harmonisation initiative represents a global collaborative effort to establish a unified, evidence-based framework for the definition, diagnosis, grading, and management of ACLF. Building on the strengths of existing regional definitions and integrating diverse international perspectives, this consensus provides a pragmatic, globally applicable foundation for clinical practice, research, and education. It also establishes a common framework for patient stratification, organ dysfunction and failure assessment, critical care management, liver transplantation, and the design of future phase II/III trials. Standardised, regulatory-aligned endpoints are expected to improve cross-study comparability, strengthen collaboration, and accelerate development of effective ACLF therapies.
items.authors: European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL)

items.title: Intralesional cemiplimab for patients with early-stage cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma: Results from a dose-escalation study with expansion cohorts.

sections.objective: Non-surgical treatment of patients with early-stage (1-2 cm diameter) cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) remains an unmet need. This study investigates low-dose intralesional cemiplimab for these patients. The primary objective was safety of low-dose intralesional cemiplimab. Efficacy was a secondary objective.
sections.methods: This was an open-label, phase 1 pilot study with dose escalation and expansion cohorts (NCT03889912). One lesion was injected per patient. Cemiplimab was initially administered at 5, 15, and 44 mg weekly, for 12 weeks. Subsequently, Expansion Cohorts A and B received 5 mg intralesional cemiplimab weekly or every 2 weeks, respectively, for 6 weeks. Visual response assessments were performed at Weeks 7 and 13, and surgery at Week 13.
sections.results: Across 41 patients, cemiplimab showed an acceptable safety profile. In Expansion Cohorts A and B, treatment-emergent adverse events were all grade ≤2. Week 13 visual and pathologic complete response rates were both 58.3% in Cohort A and 41.7% and 66.7%, respectively, in Cohort B.
sections.conclusion: Low-dose intralesional cemiplimab demonstrated efficacy against early-stage CSCC, with an acceptable safety profile. These data support further study of 5 mg intralesional cemiplimab weekly.
sections.other: The small number of participants limits generalizability. Intralesional cemiplimab administration may have been variable.

items.title: 52-Week Safety and Disease Control With Ruxolitinib Cream in Children Aged 2 to 11 Years With Atopic Dermatitis: Results From the Phase 3 TRuE-AD3 Study.

sections.objective: Ruxolitinib (selective Janus kinase [JAK]1/JAK2 inhibitor) cream demonstrated efficacy and safety vs vehicle during 8 weeks of continuous use in a phase 3 study of children with atopic dermatitis (AD). To evaluate long-term safety (LTS) and disease control with as-needed ruxolitinib cream use in children.
sections.methods: Children aged 2-11 years with mild-to-moderate AD initially randomized to ruxolitinib cream (0.75% or 1.5%) in the 8-week study continued the same twice-daily (BID) regimen for an additional 44 weeks but only applied cream as needed BID; patients initially on vehicle were rerandomized (1:1) to apply either ruxolitinib cream strength as needed. Safety and disease control were assessed.
sections.results: No new safety signals emerged among children who applied ruxolitinib cream in the LTS period (N=282). Application site reactions were infrequent (1.1%), and no serious treatment-related adverse events were observed. Among patients initially randomized to ruxolitinib cream (0.75%/1.5%), disease control was maintained to Week 52 (Investigator's Global Assessment score 0/1, 79.5%/72.3%; affected body surface area, 2.0%/1.9%).
sections.conclusion: Ruxolitinib cream applied as needed over 44 weeks was well tolerated and demonstrated disease control in children aged 2-11 years, consistent with findings in adolescents and adults.
sections.other: No vehicle control in LTS period.

items.title: Contralateral Major Amputation Following Diabetes- and Peripheral Artery Disease-Related Limb Loss: A Systematic Review and Pooled Meta-Analysis.

sections.objective: Major amputation remains a devastating and understudied outcome in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and diabetes mellitus (DM)-related limb disease. Although modern vascular care emphasizes index and symptomatic limb surveillance, the population-level risk of non-index limb (NIL) major amputation remains incompletely defined. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to quantify NIL major amputation incidence and evaluate factors associated with contralateral limb loss.
sections.methods: A systematic search of PubMed (MEDLINE), Embase, and Scopus through January 2026 was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Studies reporting contralateral above- or below-knee amputation in adults with PAD, CLTI, DM-related limb disease, or prior ipsilateral major amputation were included. Single-arm random-effects meta-analysis using the restricted maximum likelihood (REML) estimator was performed with log-transformed effect sizes. Subgroup analyses were conducted by clinical phenotype, geographic location, study era, and DM prevalence. Secondary outcomes included overall mortality, bilateral major amputation, NIL minor amputation, NIL revascularization, and development of NIL CLTI.
sections.results: Seventeen cohorts encompassing 30,359 patients were included. The pooled incidence of NIL major amputation was 6 per 100 person-years (95% CI, 3-9), with substantial heterogeneity (I2=98.93%). Meta-regression showed no significant differences by clinical phenotype (P=.622), geographic region (P=.662), study era (P=.893), or DM prevalence (P=.127). Clinical phenotypes included CLTI versus non-CLTI PAD or DM versus post-ipsilateral major amputation. Geographic region was divided into United States and international studies. Study era was divided into modern (2010-2025) and legacy (pre-2010) studies. Longer follow-up duration was inversely associated with reported incidence (P<.001). Pooled mortality rate was 38% (95% CI, 30-47%), and the pooled rate of bilateral major amputation was 12% (95% CI, 8-18%). Other secondary outcomes included a pooled NIL minor amputation rate of 11% (95% CI, 3-37%), NIL revascularization rate of 19% (95% CI, 6-47%), and NIL CLTI development rate of 32% (95% CI, 11-64%).
sections.conclusion: NIL major amputation remains a persistent risk in PAD and DM-related limb disease. These findings support the need for structured bilateral limb surveillance and early NIL risk stratification to inform comprehensive limb preservation care.

items.title: Index Below-Knee Endovascular Intervention for Intermittent Claudication Is Associated with Increased Amputation Risk.

sections.objective: Guidelines advise against infrapopliteal peripheral vascular intervention (PVI) for intermittent claudication (IC) due to potential harm with unclear benefit. We hypothesized that below-knee intervention at index PVI for IC confers higher future amputation risk than above-knee-only treatment.
sections.methods: From the VQI PVI registry (2015-2025), we identified elective, initial PVIs for IC and compared those patients undergoing above-knee-only treatment (AK) to those having any below-knee intervention (BK). Using our previously described methodology, long-term amputation data were obtained by linking the PVI and amputation registries via unique patient identifiers. Demographic and procedural data were analyzed descriptively. Kaplan-Meier Analysis estimated risk of major and any (major+minor) amputation, with independent predictors of amputation identified by multivariable Firth logistic regression.
sections.results: Among 92,899 treated limbs (81,338 AK; 11,561 BK), BK patients had increased rates of diabetes (54% vs. 41%), CHF (18% vs. 13%), and ESRD/dialysis (4.7% vs. 1.7%, p<0.001). BK patients were more likely to be Black (21% vs. 13%, p<0.001), Hispanic (8.8% vs. 4.3%, p<0.001), and Asian (1.5% vs. 1.0%, p<0.001). Smoking history predominated in AK (89% vs. 67%, p<0.001). 16,086 limbs required repeat PVI, 13,831 (17%) in the AK group vs. 2,255 (20%) in the BK group (p<0.001). At reintervention, BK patients were more likely to have progressed to CLTI (41% vs. 25%; p<0.001) and undergo ≥2 repeat interventions (32% vs. 27%; p<0.001). Initial below-knee intervention was associated with greater ipsilateral major (OR 2.39;1.70-3.35) and any (OR 2.36;1.75-3.18) amputation. Kaplan-Meier showed increased major [1-year (0.3% vs 0.1%);5-years (0.4% vs 0.1%)] and any amputation risk [1-year (0.5% vs 0.1%); 5-years (0.7% vs 0.2%).
sections.conclusion: Index below-knee intervention for IC portends greater risk of progression to CLTI, repeat PVI, and ipsilateral amputation, highlighting the potentially dangerous treatment trap of infrapopliteal intervention in patients with intermittent claudicants.

items.title: The neurobiology of menopause: Implications for brain aging and Alzheimer's risk.
items.abstract: A growing body of evidence implicates the menopausal transition as a neurobiological inflection point in women's brain aging and Alzheimer's disease (AD) vulnerability. Menopause is a midlife neuroendocrine transition characterized by a decline in sex steroid hormones and widespread systemic effects. The brain is not a passive recipient of ovarian hormones but an active endocrine-sensing organ. Menopause, however, does not act in isolation: the ovarian-brain axis is established embryonically, activated at puberty, remodeled during pregnancy and postpartum, and reconfigured during the menopausal transition, with implications for later-life brain aging. This review places menopause within a lifespan neuroendocrine framework, examining mechanisms by which the transition may influence the brain, including altered hormone signaling, bioenergetics, synaptic plasticity, neurovascular function, inflammation, and AD-related pathology. It then reviews evidence linking menopausal timing to neurobiological and AD vulnerability, discusses estrogen therapy, and considers menopause as a biologically plausible window for risk stratification and prevention.

items.title: Pharmacological treatment of patent ductus arteriosus and mortality risk in preterm infants: a Bayesian meta-analysis across gestational age groups.

sections.objective: Recent randomised controlled trials and meta-analyses have questioned the safety of early pharmacological treatment of patent ductus arteriosus in preterm infants, suggesting possible increases in the risk of mortality and bronchopulmonary dysplasia. Whether these risks vary by gestational age remains uncertain. We aimed to compare the effects of pharmacological patent ductus arteriosus treatment in infants with a gestational age less than 26 weeks versus those with a gestational age of 26 weeks or greater.
sections.methods: For this Bayesian model-averaged meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) for randomised controlled trials enrolling infants with a gestational age less than 32 weeks and echocardiographically confirmed patent ductus arteriosus who were randomly assigned either to pharmacological treatment or to placebo or expectant management. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality before 36 weeks' postmenstrual age and secondary outcomes were moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia and the composite of death or moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs) were estimated. RRs greater than 1 indicated harm. We calculated the posterior probability of harm (Prharm=P[logRR>0]) and Bayes factors comparing harm versus benefit (BFharm/benefit). This study is registered on PROSPERO (CRD42024622527).
sections.results: Ten randomised controlled trials including 2365 infants (1133 female and 1232 male) were analysed; 1045 had a gestational age less than 26 weeks. Pharmacological treatment was associated with increased mortality in infants with a gestational age less than 26 weeks (RR 1·12 [95% CrI 0·90-1·41], Prharm=0·85, BFharm/benefit=5·48), in those with a gestational age of 26 weeks or greater (1·22 [0·90-1·77], Prharm=0·89, BFharm/benefit=7·82), and in the overall population (1·23 [95% CrI 1·00-1·54], Prharm=0·97, BFharm/benefit=36·04). For bronchopulmonary dysplasia and the composite outcome of death or moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia, analyses explicitly incorporating the possibility of no effect indicated that the data were more consistent with the no-effect model than with either the benefit or the harm model.
sections.conclusion: The currently available randomised evidence is consistent with an increased mortality risk associated with pharmacological patent ductus arteriosus treatment, without evidence of a compensatory reduction in bronchopulmonary dysplasia. This association was evident both below and above the 26-week gestational age threshold. These findings question the safety of routine pharmacological treatment and underscore the need for more selective, evidence-based approaches for patent ductus arteriosus management.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of oral orforglipron in Japanese participants with obesity disease (ATTAIN-J): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: Orforglipron, a small-molecule, non-peptide, oral GLP-1 receptor agonist, has shown bodyweight reduction and cardiometabolic benefits in adults with obesity across phase 3 trials globally. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of orforglipron versus placebo for treating obesity disease in Japanese adults.
sections.methods: ATTAIN-J was a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial conducted across 16 medical research centres and hospitals in Japan and included adults aged 18 years or older with a BMI between 27 kg/m2 and less than 35 kg/m2 and two or more obesity-related health disorders, or a BMI of 35 kg/m2 or higher and one or more obesity-related health disorder, with one or more of the obesity-related health disorders being hypertension, dyslipidaemia, or type 2 diabetes (targeted at about 25% of participants), consistent with Japanese indications for tirzepatide and semaglutide for obesity disease; and at least one unsuccessful dietary attempt to lose weight. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) via a computer-generated sequence to once-daily oral orforglipron (6 mg, 12 mg, or 36 mg) or placebo. Co-primary endpoints were mean percentage change in bodyweight and percentage of participants with at least 5% bodyweight reduction from baseline to week 72. Efficacy endpoints were primarily evaluated by the treatment regimen estimand in all randomly assigned participants. Safety was assessed in participants who received at least one dose of study treatment. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05931380 (completed).
sections.results: Between July 31, 2023, and June 19, 2025, 291 participants were screened, of whom 238 (144 [61%] males and 94 [39%] females; mean age 54·1 years [SD 11·2]) were randomly assigned to receive orforglipron 6 mg (n=61), 12 mg (n=57), or 36 mg (n=60), or placebo (n=60); 214 (90%) participants completed the study. At week 72, mean percentage change in bodyweight was -5·9% (95% CI -7·6 to -4·2) with orforglipron 6 mg, -8·7% (-10·9 to -6·5) with 12 mg, and -7·9% (-10·0 to -5·8) with 36 mg, compared with -0·6% (-2·1 to 0·8) with placebo (all p<0·0001 vs placebo). At week 72, a bodyweight reduction of at least 5% was seen in 15·2% (SE 4·8; nine of 60) of participants in the placebo group compared with 45·6% (6·1; 28 of 61; p=0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 6 mg group, 60·8% (6·4; 35 of 57; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 12 mg group, and 58·8% (6·5; 35 of 60; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 36 mg group. Adverse events with orforglipron were mostly mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal symptoms. Across all orforglipron groups, treatment-emergent adverse events that most frequently led to study treatment discontinuation were nausea (one [2%] of 61 in the 6 mg group, one [2%] of 57 in the 12 mg group, and five [8%] of 60 in the 36 mg group vs none with placebo) and vomiting (none in the 6 mg group, two [4%] in the 12 mg group, and one [2%] in the 36 mg group vs none in the placebo group).
sections.conclusion: In Japanese adults with obesity disease, once-daily orforglipron resulted in statistically superior reductions in bodyweight versus placebo, with a safety profile consistent with that of other GLP-1 receptor agonists.
sections.other: For the Japanese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

items.title: Clinical and metabolic subtypes of recent-onset adult type 1 diabetes: a prospective cohort study.

sections.objective: Adult-onset type 1 diabetes exhibits substantial heterogeneity. We aimed to investigate whether this variability reflects distinct disease entities or different temporal stages of a shared autoimmune process.
sections.methods: In this prospective cohort study, we analysed data from adults (aged 18-69 years) in the German Diabetes Study who had clinically diagnosed type 1 diabetes within the preceding 12 months, and from individuals who were positive for glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody (GADA) but had originally been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. We used unsupervised machine learning based on GADA status, fasting C-peptide, glucose, triglycerides, and HDL cholesterol to characterise clinical and metabolic type 1 diabetes subtypes. The resulting subtypes were compared for aetiological traits (polygenic risk scores for type 1 diabetes and type 2 diabetes, partitioned type 2 diabetes polygenic risk scores, human leukocyte antigen [HLA] profiles, and islet-directed autoantibodies), insulin sensitivity, glucagon-stimulated C-peptide trajectories as a measure of residual β-cell function, and complications during prospective follow-up. Reproducibility was assessed in adults with type 1 diabetes from the German Diabetes Prospective Follow-up Registry (Diabetes-Patienten-Verlaufsdokumentation [DPV]).
sections.results: Analysed participants in the German Diabetes Study cohort were recruited between June 27, 2005, and Jan 20, 2025 (n=600), and were followed up for a mean of 6·1 (SD 4·7) years. We identified three type 1 diabetes subtypes: two GADA-positive subtypes, and one GADA-negative subtype. A similar clinical and metabolic subtype structure was observed in the DPV cohort, whose participants were recruited between 2000 and 2025 (n=483) and were followed up for a mean of 3·1 (SD 5·0) years. One GADA-positive subtype was characterised by lower BMI, higher insulin sensitivity, and severe β-cell dysfunction (classic type 1 diabetes), whereas the second showed higher BMI, lower insulin sensitivity, and better β-cell function (mixed type 1 diabetes). The two GADA-positive subtypes did not differ in autoimmunity or type 1 diabetes polygenic risk scores, whereas the GADA-negative subtype had lower genetic type 1 diabetes risk, despite no clear subtype-specific differences in HLA risk haplotypes. Longitudinal modelling indicated that the mixed type 1 diabetes group was positioned 6·1 years (95% CI 4·6-7·8) earlier along the β-cell function decline trajectory compared with the classic type 1 diabetes group. The risks of hypoglycaemia (log-rank p=0·0019), retinopathy (mixed type 1 diabetes vs classic type 1 diabetes: adjusted hazard ratio 4·93 [95% CI 1·71-14·24]), and cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy (log-rank p=0·028) differed across the groups.
sections.conclusion: Our results indicate that individuals with combined autoimmunity and lower insulin sensitivity present with clinical diabetes earlier than classic type 1 diabetes along the β-cell decline trajectory, identifying a potential timeframe for disease-modifying interventions in specific type 1 diabetes subtypes.
sections.other: For the German translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

items.title: Performance of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways in patients with suspected myocardial infarction: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

sections.objective: In patients with suspected myocardial infarction, the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) is recommended in current guidelines for early risk stratification. However, individual trials used different safety outcomes, and efficacy outcomes were inconclusive or not assessed. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of all randomised controlled trials to synthesise the totality of the evidence, assess heterogeneity across trials, and evaluate clinically relevant outcomes using harmonised definitions across trials.
sections.methods: In this systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform from inception to July 6, 2026, without language restrictions, for randomised trials comparing the safety and efficacy of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h, ie, standard care). Individual participant data were obtained and outcome definitions were harmonised. The primary analysis used a two-stage random-effects meta-analysis. After receipt of the individual participant data but before data harmonisation or analysis, the primary safety outcome was refined to a composite of all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, from the originally specified composite of all-cause death or any new myocardial infarction. The primary efficacy outcomes were emergency department length of stay and direct discharge from the emergency department. This meta-analysis is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383452).
sections.results: Our systematic review identified five randomised trials, all of which provided individual participant data. Among these, the definition of the primary safety outcome varied, and in four trials emergency department length of stay was not reported for the whole analysis population. We included 110 933 patient presentations (55 489 managed with the 0/1 h pathway and 55 444 managed with the 0/3 h pathway). Within 30 days, all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 446 patient presentations (0·8%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 562 patient presentations (1·0%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled odds ratio [OR] 0·83 [95% CI 0·45-1·53]; I2=62·9%; τ2=0·143). Emergency department length of stay was 314 min (IQR 211-481) in the 0/1 h pathway group versus 308 min (209-453) in the 0/3 h pathway group (random-effects pooled geometric mean ratio 1·03 [95% CI 0·85-1·25]; I2=99·2%; τ2=0·024). Direct discharge from the emergency department occurred in 37 190 patient presentations (67·0%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 36 485 patient presentations (65·8%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled OR 1·31 [95% CI 0·79-2·16]; I2=97·8%; τ2=0·156).
sections.conclusion: Across the available randomised trials, short-term adverse event rates were low with both pathways, but the pooled safety estimate remained imprecise. On average, earlier cardiac troponin retesting did not reduce emergency department length of stay or clearly increase direct discharge, and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicates that treatment effects might not translate uniformly across health-care systems. For hospitals considering transitioning from a 0/3 h to a 0/1 h pathway, implementation decisions should take broader diagnostic and organisational considerations into account.

items.title: Irritable bowel syndrome and related disorders of gut-brain interaction.
items.abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea are disorders of gut-brain interaction, the symptoms of which include abnormal stool consistency or frequency accompanied by varying degrees of abdominal pain, discomfort, bloating, or distension. These conditions affect 20% of the global population with a relapsing and remitting course. Risk factors include female sex, younger age, a history of common mental disorders, and acute enteric infection. The pathophysiology of irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea remain incompletely understood, but are thought to be secondary to aberrant interactions throughout the gut-brain axis, resulting in disordered gut motility and visceral hypersensitivity. These conditions are diagnosed with a combination of clinical history, absence of alarm symptoms-such as weight loss or rectal bleeding-and targeted investigations. An empathetic management approach improves quality of life and symptoms, reduces health-care use, and enhances treatment adherence. Mainstays of treatment include education, dietary and lifestyle advice, modifying fibre intake, and drugs directed towards predominant symptoms. For severe symptoms, other treatments include specific medical devices, biofeedback, or psychological therapies. However, the effectiveness of most treatments is modest and there is an ongoing need to expand available treatments for bowel disorders, with several novel drugs currently in development.

items.title: Genetic coupling of floral rewards and signals underlies pollinator attraction.
items.abstract: Animal pollinators underpin biodiversity and global agriculture, yet the molecular mechanisms that coordinate floral rewards and signals to attract pollinators remain poorly understood.
